Canterbury Station and the Kensington Shipping Platform both orbit the planet, generating a considerable amount of traffic. Since the end of the Gallic War, considerable amounts of radioactive battle debris have fallen into the gas giant's atmosphere. Local companies have urged the Bretonian government to take immediate action before the wreckage forms a ring system that could imperil local shipping, however little has been done so far.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: New London -> Manchester
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>A jump gate is a conveyance technology that allows instantaneous travel between two distinct points in space using technology pioneered by Ageira Technologies and built by Deep Space Engineering in 130 AS. objects.name: Dublin Drive Breach
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TRA data="65281" mask="-31" def="30"/><TEXT>***GRAVITATIONAL ANOMALY DETECTED***</TEXT><PARA/><TRA data="96" mask="-31" def="-1"/><TEXT> </TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>Magnetic and gravimetric readings are consistent with a Jump Hole -- a natural phenomenon that functions similar to a Jump Gate, though the hazards associated with traveling through a Jump Hole remain largely unknown. Like Jump Gates, jump holes are semi-permeable areas in real-space that have a tendency to breach the natural boundaries of linear time and space. Unlike Jump Gates, though, these anomalies occur naturally and so are both unpredictable and unstable. Traveling through jump holes is a risky proposition at best. Though some have been charted and, based on accounts from ships that have accidentally encountered them, have had their exit points logged, just as many ships have never been heard from again. It is believed that these ships were either crushed in the violent, cataclysmic vortex that lies outside the narrow corridor of a jump tunnel, or were sent to a place far enough away to make communication or a return trip infeasible. In either case, those missing are presumed dead. Ageira Technologies and Deep Space Engineering urge all citizens to use the prescribed Trade Lanes and Jump Gates and to avoid all contact with jump holes.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: New London Docking Ring
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TRA data="65281" mask="-31" def="30"/><TEXT>>>>WARNING: Do not attempt planetary landing without using a Docking Ring.<<<</TEXT><PARA/><TRA data="96" mask="-31" def="-1"/><TEXT> </TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>A docking ring is a piece of orbiting technology that, through the use of super strong crystalline polymers and frictionless bearings, assists the smooth atmospheric entry of any interstellar vessel that has the ability to land. Invented in 130 AS by Ageira Technologies, these 'orbital elevators' almost completely negate the cost of boosting people or materials out of a planetary gravity well. Docking rings revolutionized exploration and industry almost overnight, opening up entire systems for commercial exploration and exploitation.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>Ageira Technologies licenses this technology to the other houses, who in turn agree to design all ships (except for special exploratory and survey vessels), to work with the docking ring system.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Planet Wight
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>DIAMETER: 12,220 km</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>MASS: 5.66 x 10e24 kg</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>TERRAIN: Ice</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>TEMPERATURE: -92°C to -64°C</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>ESCAPE VELOCITY: 11.27 km/sec</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT> </TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>A frozen planet locked in a deep crust of ice. Scientists theorize that Wight might once have supported life until its atmosphere was ripped away during an ancient catastrophe. Today, Birmingham Station orbits Wight, and due to the loss of the Ayr project in Edinburgh, and the closing of other Bretonian projects, the government has granted Planetform the contract to initiate terraforming on Wight. The planet is situated close to a high concentration of readily available ice from the Barrier, and logistically the project has advantages. That being said, the nearby Gaian base has stepped up operations in Manchester to disrupt the project, as they have historically done so in Edinburgh and Tau-31.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Planet Jersey
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>DIAMETER: 9,348 km</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>MASS: 3.83 x 10e24 kg</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>TERRAIN: Ice</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>TEMPERATURE: -88°C to -60°C</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>ESCAPE VELOCITY: 8.42 km/sec</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT> </TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>An icy, airless planet. Initial surveys found no mineral or gas deposits of any size worth exploiting, while the environment was inhospitable to colonization.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TRA data="1" mask="1" def="-2"/><JUST loc="center"/><TEXT>WENDIGOS</TEXT><PARA/><TRA data="0" mask="1" def="-1"/><JUST loc="left"/><PARA/><TEXT>Wendigos serve the aliens known as the Vagrants. A Wendigo Infiltrator is controlled by a parasitic creature known as an "incubus", which can override the host's every action. Most Wendigos are not directly infected, instead being psychically indoctrinated Thralls that execute their masters' plots. There is no known way to remove an uncooperative incubus without killing the host, and captured Wendigos of either category will fight to the death rather than submit to interrogation. Study of the remains may yield insight into the process by which infestation and indoctrination occurs.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TRA data="1" mask="1" def="-2"/><JUST loc="center"/><TEXT>Properties</TEXT><PARA/><TRA data="0" mask="1" def="-1"/><PARA/><JUST loc="left"/><TEXT>Base Price: $50</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>Container Hitpoints: 1000</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>Cargo Space Per Unit: 1</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Interlocutor
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>This Prosecutor has been set down in the dust of an asteroid's crater. While the vessel's name is emblazoned on its flanks, the onboard nav computer and transponder has been thoroughly purged. There is no sign of battle damage or mechanical malfunction, however scans indicate the pilot remains in the cockpit.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Manchester -> New London
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>A jump gate is a conveyance technology that allows instantaneous travel between two distinct points in space using technology pioneered by Ageira Technologies and built by Deep Space Engineering in 130 AS. According to the annual Ageira Technologies Shareholder Report, 'jump gate technology is designed to gather and amplify certain permeable tendencies in real-space and connect them to other congruent points elsewhere in the sector, while still maintaining the structural integrity and stability of the channel created by this process and of the object passing through it.'</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>Ageira Technologies and Deep Space Engineering continue to survey other potential jump point candidates and expect to provide connections with other areas further and further away as their research continues.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Newcastle Jump Hole
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TRA data="65281" mask="-31" def="30"/><TEXT>***GRAVITATIONAL ANOMALY DETECTED***</TEXT><PARA/><TRA data="96" mask="-31" def="-1"/><TEXT> </TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>Magnetic and gravimetric readings are consistent with a Jump Hole -- a natural phenomenon that functions similar to a Jump Gate, though the hazards associated with traveling through a Jump Hole remain largely unknown. Like Jump Gates, jump holes are semi-permeable areas in real-space that have a tendency to breach the natural boundaries of linear time and space. Unlike Jump Gates, though, these anomalies occur naturally and so are both unpredictable and unstable. Traveling through jump holes is a risky proposition at best. Though some have been charted and, based on accounts from ships that have accidentally encountered them, have had their exit points logged, just as many ships have never been heard from again. It is believed that these ships were either crushed in the violent, cataclysmic vortex that lies outside the narrow corridor of a jump tunnel, or were sent to a place far enough away to make communication or a return trip infeasible. In either case, those missing are presumed dead. Ageira Technologies and Deep Space Engineering urge all citizens to use the prescribed Trade Lanes and Jump Gates and to avoid all contact with jump holes.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Liverpool Wreck
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>CLASS: Eden</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>GRAVITY: None</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>DOCKING: No</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>AMENITIES: N/A</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>CREW: 0</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>The remnants of the Liverpool Border Station, which served as a coordination center and crew base for the Bretonia Police Authority in the Manchester system. During its operation, service at this station was considered a matter of great pride, with many families providing multiple generations of constables. In 829 AS, Liverpool was adopted as a staging post for the Armed Forces task force dispatched to aid the Liberty Navy with their campaign against the Insurgency.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>The station's proud tradition was abruptly ended later that same year when the reactor was sabotaged, resulting in the loss of nearly two-thirds of the crew. Although the Mollys initially claimed responsibility for the attack, BPA investigators later dismissed this as incompatible with recovered evidence. Reconstructed security footage indicated that hacked service droids may have played a role in the attack, pointing the finger at either the Technocracy or Lane Hackers.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>DIAMETER: 200 km</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>MASS: 0.66 x 10e20 kg</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>TERRAIN: N/A</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>TEMPERATURE: N/A</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>ESCAPE VELOCITY: N/A</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT> </TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>Smaller than some asteroids, the Ross Planetoid exists at a gravitational sink where ice fragments have collected over the millennia and begun to compact under their own weight into the seed of what might eventually become a planet. objects.name: New London Jump Hole
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TRA data="65281" mask="-31" def="30"/><TEXT>***GRAVITATIONAL ANOMALY DETECTED***</TEXT><PARA/><TRA data="96" mask="-31" def="-1"/><TEXT> </TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>Magnetic and gravimetric readings are consistent with a Jump Hole -- a natural phenomenon that functions similar to a Jump Gate, though the hazards associated with traveling through a Jump Hole remain largely unknown. Like Jump Gates, jump holes are semi-permeable areas in real-space that have a tendency to breach the natural boundaries of linear time and space. Unlike Jump Gates, though, these anomalies occur naturally and so are both unpredictable and unstable. Traveling through jump holes is a risky proposition at best. Though some have been charted and, based on accounts from ships that have accidentally encountered them, have had their exit points logged, just as many ships have never been heard from again. It is believed that these ships were either crushed in the violent, cataclysmic vortex that lies outside the narrow corridor of a jump tunnel, or were sent to a place far enough away to make communication or a return trip infeasible. In either case, those missing are presumed dead. Ageira Technologies and Deep Space Engineering urge all citizens to use the prescribed Trade Lanes and Jump Gates and to avoid all contact with jump holes.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Cambridge Docking Ring
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TRA data="65281" mask="-31" def="30"/><TEXT>>>>WARNING: Do not attempt planetary landing without using a Docking Ring.<<<</TEXT><PARA/><TRA data="96" mask="-31" def="-1"/><TEXT> </TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>A docking ring is a piece of orbiting technology that, through the use of super strong crystalline polymers and frictionless bearings, assists the smooth atmospheric entry of any interstellar vessel that has the ability to land. Invented in 130 AS by Ageira Technologies, these 'orbital elevators' almost completely negate the cost of boosting people or materials out of a planetary gravity well. Docking rings revolutionized exploration and industry almost overnight, opening up entire systems for commercial exploration and exploitation.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>Ageira Technologies licenses this technology to the other houses, who in turn agree to design all ships (except for special exploratory and survey vessels), to work with the docking ring system.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Leeds Monument
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><PARA/><TEXT>Following the conclusion of the Gallic War, a group of citizens, corporations, and public entities under the name of the Leeds Restoration League gathered to construct a war memorial to honor all who died in service to Bretonia during the war, soldiers and civilians alike. Constructed with shards of Leeds soil glass and salvaged station parts from the system's destroyed stations, the monument has engraved on its exterior a poem, written by Bretonian poet laureate Guinevere Mitchell. Inside the memorial is a radio transmitter, powered by the radioactivity of harvested toxic waste from the system's smog clouds, which repeatedly broadcasts an audio recording of Mitchell reciting the poem. The signal is strong enough to be detected by ships passing close to the planet's orbit.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TRA data="1" mask="1" def="-2"/><TEXT>A Hymn to Leeds</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TRA data="0" mask="0" def="-1"/><TEXT>In the ashes below lies a city in pieces,</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>cut by a furious blade.</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>Roiling earth and a sky of shadows</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>and plains of lifeless glass</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>form humanity's foulest grave.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>But around us, see our finest work,</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>thought it has yet to be done.</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>Hail Bretonia! May her banner fly,</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>but never flee,</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>'round every ship and sun.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>We find ourselves in Leeds,</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>but where her heart is laid to rest,</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>our hearts,</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>broken,</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>may heal.</TEXT><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: New London Jump Hole
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TRA data="65281" mask="-31" def="30"/><TEXT>***GRAVITATIONAL ANOMALY DETECTED***</TEXT><PARA/><TRA data="96" mask="-31" def="-1"/><TEXT> </TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>Magnetic and gravimetric readings are consistent with a Jump Hole -- a natural phenomenon that functions similar to a Jump Gate, though the hazards associated with traveling through a Jump Hole remain largely unknown. Like Jump Gates, jump holes are semi-permeable areas in real-space that have a tendency to breach the natural boundaries of linear time and space. Unlike Jump Gates, though, these anomalies occur naturally and so are both unpredictable and unstable. Traveling through jump holes is a risky proposition at best. Though some have been charted and, based on accounts from ships that have accidentally encountered them, have had their exit points logged, just as many ships have never been heard from again. It is believed that these ships were either crushed in the violent, cataclysmic vortex that lies outside the narrow corridor of a jump tunnel, or were sent to a place far enough away to make communication or a return trip infeasible. In either case, those missing are presumed dead. Ageira Technologies and Deep Space Engineering urge all citizens to use the prescribed Trade Lanes and Jump Gates and to avoid all contact with jump holes.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

Officer Sandra Bassett

objects.name: Battleship Hood
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>CLASS: Victoria (Derelict)</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>DOCKING: No</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>Amenities: No</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>CREW: 0</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>Originally the lead ship of the Bretonian Armed Forces' response to the Founder's Day Revolt in 752 AS, the Hood's engines were struck by a huge Molly mine and disabled. The battleship was deemed too unstable to make the jump to New London for repairs, and was officially scuttled once its weaponry, armor and valuable subsystems were stripped. </TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>The Hood remained an abandoned hulk for decades, until it was re-pressurized by enterprising members of the Independent Miners Guild in 778 AS as a base for their own Gold extraction operations. While acting as a floating bazaar, it served as the only operational Freeport within House space. Due to this, the Hood was also of critical importance to the Mollys, as one of the few places they could exchange their Gold for necessary supplies.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>Over time, the Hood developed an infamous reputation from its disreputable clientele and the popular race track in the nearby asteroid field. This dangerous circuit would more often result in a survivor than a winner, attracting a subculture of gamblers and adrenaline junkies to the system.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>Following Bretonia's withdrawal from Dublin in 831 AS, Corsair raiders began to launch large scale incursions into the system, significantly escalating their conflict with the Mollys. After suffering unexpectedly heavy casualties, the Battlecruiser Santander destroyed the Hood as a calculated strategy to starve the Mollys into submission through a blockade. This strategy has had limited success, despite imposing a heavy toll on both groups.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Jatibonico
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>The Jatibonico was a Coalition Typhoon class cruiser, assigned to the Molly's Powrie Brigade. She served across the Omegas and Rheinland, notably participating in the breaching of Vierlande Prison and reprisal attacks on the Unioners. The Jatibonico was destroyed in Dublin by the Battlecruiser Adlington, shortly before its own destruction.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Damuji
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>The Damuji was a Coalition Typhoon class cruiser, assigned to the Molly's Powrie Brigade. She served across the Omegas, seeing combat against the Corsairs, The Core, and the Bretonian Armed Forces during their occupation of Planet Gran Canaria. The Damuji was destroyed in Dublin during battle with the Bretonian Fifth Royal Cruiser Flotilla.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Gobnait
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>The Gobnait was a Molly Hel class cruiser, assigned to the Powrie Brigade. She was purchased from the Red Hessians shortly before the Bretonian invasion of Dublin. The Gobnait was destroyed in Dublin during battle with the Bretonian Fifth Royal Cruiser Flotilla.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Ballingarry
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>The Ballingarry was a Molly Scylla class cruiser, assigned to the Sluagh Brigade. She was purchased from the Liberty Rogues in 832 AS, and smuggled into Dublin to resist the pending Bretonian invasion. The Ballingarry was destroyed in Dublin during battle with the Bretonian First Royal Cruiser Flotilla.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: O'Doherty
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>The O'Doherty was a Molly Hel class cruiser, assigned to the Sluagh Brigade. She was purchased from the Red Hessians in 827 AS, after being retired from their fleet. The O'Doherty was destroyed in Dublin during battle with the Bretonian First Royal Cruiser Flotilla.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Shannon
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>The Shannon was a Crecy class cruiser assigned to the Fifth Royal Cruiser Flotilla. She served throughout the Gallic War, and participated in the ill-fated Bretonian intervention into Vespucci during Liberty's campaign against the Insurgency. The Shannon was destroyed in Dublin with the detonation of the fire ship Fortune.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Blake
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>The Blake was a Crecy class cruiser assigned to the Fifth Royal Cruiser Flotilla. She served throughout the Gallic War, being mothballed in the aftermath until reactivated for the Invasion of Dublin. The Blake was destroyed in Dublin during battle with the Molly Powrie Brigade.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Endymion
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>The Endymion was a Agincourt class cruiser assigned to the First Royal Cruiser Flotilla. She was constructed at Portsmouth Shipyard and launched shortly prior to the Invasion of Dublin. The Endymion was destroyed in Dublin with the detonation of the fire ship Hope.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Narcissus
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>The Narcissus was a Agincourt class cruiser assigned to the First Royal Cruiser Flotilla. She served throughout the Gallic War, receiving an Agincourt upgrade package at Portsmouth Shipyard prior to the Invasion of Dublin. The Narcissus was destroyed in Dublin during battle with the Molly Sluagh Brigade.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: RNC Neuburg
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>The Nueburg is a disabled Rheinland gunship, apparently dating to a rumored raid on Dublin during the Colony Wars. The ship appears to have been destroyed when its engines were targeted. Broken and gaunt, it remains adrift near the Glorious as if an ill omen.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Blackrock
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>The wreck of the Battlecuiser Blackrock. Following the conclusion of the Gallic War, the Blackrock was redeployed to secure Bretonian interests in the Dublin system.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>With the Ark Royale being repositioned closer to Dublin, the Blackrock took the opportunity to bait the Carllion out of the asteroid field for an open engagement, to end the threat it has posed on Bretonian shipping and mining in the system. Both the Carrillion and Blackrock fleets fought to a near standstill before the Mollys of Dublin deployed their own ambush over the remnance of both forces. </TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Battlecruiser Bracknell
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>CLASS: Fortitude</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>CREW: </TEXT><TRA data="65280" mask="-32" def="31"/><TEXT>CLASSIFIED</TEXT><PARA/><TRA data="96" mask="-32" def="-1"/><TEXT>ARMAMENT: </TEXT><TRA data="65280" mask="-32" def="31"/><TEXT>CLASSIFIED</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TRA data="96" mask="-32" def="-1"/><TEXT>The Battlecruiser Bracknell was launched in 825 AS, shortly before the fall of Southampton Shipyard. It participated in the Battle of Trafalgar, the Siege of New London, the Liberation of Leeds, and later the Invasion of Edinburgh. Post-war, it was appointed to command the First Royal Cruiser Flotilla, which it led into Dublin in 835 AS. During the initial phases of the campaign, the First were dispatched to secure the perimeter of the Achill Asteroid Field, in the hope of completely severing Molly supply lines into New London. The Mollys were quick to counter-attack with an improvised fleet, including Coalition, Militant and pirate auxiliaries.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>The Bracknell initially prioritised enemy cruisers, ignoring the fleet of Asteroid Miners slowly advancing toward them; the captain had written them off as pressganged indications of the Mollys' desperation. This threat assessment quickly changed after the comm net filled with reports that the Hegemon flagged as Fortune had detonated, destroying the Battlecruiser Adlington. The flotilla began focusing their fire on the Miners, however it was too little, too late. While outside the optimal blast range, the Hegemon Hope prematurely detonated before it could be destroyed, obliterating the Bracknell's engines as it turned to flee. After several days of bloody fighting, Royal Engineer Lifters successfully towed the stricken vessel back to the Somerset.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>Urgent field assessments are ongoing to establish whether the Bracknell can be made safe to jump out of the system for evacuation to Portsmouth Shipyard. Contingency plans have been made to jettison the reactor core into the Somerset minefield, in the event of a critical integrity deterioration.</TEXT><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: New London Drive Breach
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TRA data="65281" mask="-31" def="30"/><TEXT>***GRAVITATIONAL ANOMALY DETECTED***</TEXT><PARA/><TRA data="96" mask="-31" def="-1"/><TEXT> </TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>Magnetic and gravimetric readings are consistent with a Jump Hole -- a natural phenomenon that functions similar to a Jump Gate, though the hazards associated with traveling through a Jump Hole remain largely unknown. Like Jump Gates, jump holes are semi-permeable areas in real-space that have a tendency to breach the natural boundaries of linear time and space. Unlike Jump Gates, though, these anomalies occur naturally and so are both unpredictable and unstable. Traveling through jump holes is a risky proposition at best. Though some have been charted and, based on accounts from ships that have accidentally encountered them, have had their exit points logged, just as many ships have never been heard from again. It is believed that these ships were either crushed in the violent, cataclysmic vortex that lies outside the narrow corridor of a jump tunnel, or were sent to a place far enough away to make communication or a return trip infeasible. In either case, those missing are presumed dead. Ageira Technologies and Deep Space Engineering urge all citizens to use the prescribed Trade Lanes and Jump Gates and to avoid all contact with jump holes.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Destroyed Gallic Jump Gate
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>This Gallic Jump Gate was constructed by EFL Oil & Machinery in 824 AS, when the previous Ageira Jump Gate to Leeds was disassembled and shipped away for study. After the Glassing of Leeds and the collapse of the Gallic Royal Navy in 826 AS, the Jump Gate was disabled and then stripped of its components to prevent an immediate Bretonian invasion. When Bretonia launched its assault from the Tain Asteroid Field in late 827 AS, the Gallic Enclave detonated the Jump Gate's frame to prevent its capture.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Aberdeen Wreck
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>CLASS: Eden</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>GRAVITY: No</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>DOCKING: No</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>AMENITIES: No</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>CREW: 0</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>Aberdeen Border Station was originally a Bretonia Police Authority checkpoint that constantly watched for contraband runners and eco-terrorists. During the Tau and Gallic Wars, the station was transferred to the Bretonia Armed Forces. The facility was destroyed by the Gallic Royal Navy breaching operation in 819 AS, during the Invasion of Edinburgh.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Planet Gaia
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>DIAMETER: 12,515 km</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>MASS: 5.96 x 10e24 kg</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>TERRAIN: Terrestrial</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>TEMPERATURE: -34°C to 52°C</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>ESCAPE VELOCITY: 11.01 km/sec</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>Gaia is a tropical paradise -- a rich, green world the likes of which has not been found anywhere else in Sirius. Boasting unparalleled genetic treasures, its flora, fauna, and delicately balanced ecosystems are not yet fully understood. The University of Cambridge had for over a century operated a small research outpost on the planet, collating vast gene libraries of samples. Visits to Gaia were restricted in an attempt to prevent poaching, after rumors spread of the aphrodisiac properties of many creatures. The protection of Planet Gaia is one of the central causes of both the radical Gaian ecoterrorist movement and the Green Front lobbyist group.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>In 819 AS, Edinburgh was occupied by the Gallic Royal Navy during their Invasion of Sirius. Gaia was initially ignored, used informally by Gallic officers for hunting expeditions and other frontline R&R activities. As the war progressed, Gallia's need for resources became more desperate. As a result, EFL Oil & Machinery established several mining colonies on Gaia across 825 AS, straining the uncomfortable truce with the Gaians to breaking point. During the Glassing of Leeds the following year, Gallic forces loyal to the missing King Charles began the mass relocation of Bretonian citizens to Edinburgh as a captive workforce. Gaia was appointed as the capital of the Gallic Enclave, a radical holdout of war criminals and monarchists who refused to recognize the legitimacy of the newly formed Gallic Confederacy.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>Makeshift mining colonies exploded in size as they were flooded with Bretonian slaves, Enclave soldiers, and Gallic nobles fleeing the core systems. As the Enclave initiated slash and burn clearance to create living space, the Gaians enacted a sabotage campaign in an attempt to slow the rate of devastation. The Mollys also established covert cells on Gaia, smuggling weapons to serfs in the hope of instigating a Molly-led uprising against the Gallic occupiers. Matters came to a head with the Bretonian assault into Edinburgh in 827 AS, which saw most Enclave elements routed by the Bretonia Armed Forces. Despite this, Gaia itself and Bordeaux Orbital remained in the hands of the most extreme Royalist holdouts, who refused to surrender to the approaching fleet.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>Scandal then rocked Bretonia when the Green Front leaked government cables labeled "uti possidetis" -- a plan to assault Gaia, eliminate the Royalist garrison, and take possession of the colonies. Before this plan could be enacted, Gaian saboteurs unleashed a virulent bioweapon on the Bordeaux Orbital, rapidly liquefying the Royalist crew. This horrifying fate was broadcast to the Bretonian fleet, alongside the stark warning that a failure to evacuate captive Bretonians would result in further bioweapons being unleashed on the Bretonian landing force. Caught between an outraged public and Gaian terrorism, the government conceded. While the Bordeaux Bioweapon remains deeply controversial, many Bretonians credit the Gaians with securing the rescue of Gaia's captives.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>Those Royalists that did not fight to the death during the Bretonian bombardment and landing fled into Gaia's wilderness. In the years since Gaia's abandonment, these Royalist "wildmen" have poached Gaian Wildlife, both to feed Royalist forces in nearby systems, and to sell to sympathetic Gallic nobles for supplies. The Bretonian Intelligence Service runs regular missions to Gaia's surface to hunt down Royalist camps, often with the assistance of "local guides". Limited Cambridge expeditions have also been launched to Gaia in the war's aftermath. While the planet's scars are slowly healing, academics have described the damage to certain delicate ecosystems and species as "irreparable". </TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Planet Ayr
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>DIAMETER: 13,867 km</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>MASS: 6.21 x 10e24 kg</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>TERRAIN: Transitional</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>TEMPERATURE: -86°C to -32°C</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>ESCAPE VELOCITY: 12.22 km/sec</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT> </TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>Ayr is an arid world with a thin atmosphere but an active volcanic system beneath its crust. Initial surveys showed that a considerable amount of water vapor, CO2, and other greenhouse gases remain locked in the polar ice caps, making Ayr a prime target for terraforming. Planetform, Inc. initiated first stage terraforming in 752 AS but the operation came to an abrupt halt as Gallic Navy forces invaded the system.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Bradford
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>The Bradford, a Victoria class Dunkirk ship, was an escort of the Grimsby until its demise in 827. Originally hailing from the Derby fleet, the aging Dunkirk was selected as the vanguard for the Invasion of Edinburgh due to the age of the ship.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>Facing almost certain doom upon entry, the Bradford was reduced to a skeleton crew prior to the operation. The sacrifice however would not be in vain, as the remaining ships of the Grimsby fleet entered after it, pathing the way for the eventual pacification of Edinburgh.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Grimsby
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>The Battleship Wessex was originally stationed outside the research facility Sunderland when it was first being built, but after many years it was decided that the battleship was unnecessary as the alien ruins were completely lifeless. Shortly after the Nomad War, however, it was decided to station the newly commissioned Grimsby nearby to reassure the public.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>Many of the scientists initially objected to having a heavily armed battleship keeping watch over Sunderland, but in recent times strange raids by unidentified hostile ships has persuaded a lot of the protestors to accept the military guard force as a neccesity.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>At the end of the Gallic invasion, the Grimsby and her escorts were been diverted to Leeds in order to secure Bretonia's route to Tau space. Like most of the Bretonia Armed Forces, Grimsby's fleet is operating well below full strength, but the crew are confident they can handle whatever might oppose them.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>The Grimsby was to take part in the invasion of Edinburgh in late 827, facing the majority of the fighting around the Leeds entry point, and suffering disproportionate casualties as a result. The Grimby was lost with all hands in the fighting.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Hornsea
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>The Hornsea was an escort of the Grimsby until its untimely demise in Edinburgh in 827. Together with the Grimsby and Rutland it succeeded in breaching the first layer of defenses following the sacrifice of the aged Bradford. Together with the Grimsby it was succesful in holding the La Riche and Dax fleets around the Leeds hole, while the Macduff and Ark Royal arrived to force the Gallic Royal Navy to pull back to the safety of their final lines at Gaia. The Hornsea, like other Grimsby vessels, took the brunt of the fighting, and would not survive the battle.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: La Riche
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>A rear-echelon warship for the entirety of the Second Gallic Civil War, some of the Gallic Navy's more hardened leaders lament that the La Riche survived instead of a seasoned warship such as the Embrun or Beuvray in her place. objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>The Chartes was an escort of the La Riche. objects.name: Middlesbrough
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>A volcanic moon of Planet Carlisle, Middlesbrough's surface is a wracked by earthquakes and volcanic eruptions. The moon first came to BMM's attention in 671 AS, after it was found these chaotic conditions regularly churned rich mineral deposits to the surface. After an ownership dispute with the IMG was resolved in 678 AS, BMM begun deploying automated miners to crawl the perimeter of vast magma oceans. Cargo was then boosted into orbit to the nearby Belfast Production Facility. The platforms were lost along with Belfast itself in 814 AS, after a crew mutiny seized control of the station and handed it to the Mollys.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>Following Belfast's destruction during the Gallic War, Bretonia moved quickly to re-secure its hold over the moon. By 827 AS, Redcarr had been constructed in orbit, and a number of mining crawlers were repaired. This work was significantly complicated by unexploded mines in orbit, the remnants of the Molly minefield used for Belfast's defense. Middlesbrough has received significant state investment in the years following the war, with Bretonia hoping the moon's resources can sustain its faltering economy.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Manchester Jump Hole
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TRA data="65281" mask="-31" def="30"/><TEXT>***GRAVITATIONAL ANOMALY DETECTED***</TEXT><PARA/><TRA data="96" mask="-31" def="-1"/><TEXT> </TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>Magnetic and gravimetric readings are consistent with a Jump Hole -- a natural phenomenon that functions similar to a Jump Gate, though the hazards associated with traveling through a Jump Hole remain largely unknown. Like Jump Gates, jump holes are semi-permeable areas in real-space that have a tendency to breach the natural boundaries of linear time and space. Unlike Jump Gates, though, these anomalies occur naturally and so are both unpredictable and unstable. Traveling through jump holes is a risky proposition at best. Though some have been charted and, based on accounts from ships that have accidentally encountered them, have had their exit points logged, just as many ships have never been heard from again. It is believed that these ships were either crushed in the violent, cataclysmic vortex that lies outside the narrow corridor of a jump tunnel, or were sent to a place far enough away to make communication or a return trip infeasible. In either case, those missing are presumed dead. Ageira Technologies and Deep Space Engineering urge all citizens to use the prescribed Trade Lanes and Jump Gates and to avoid all contact with jump holes.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Fort Albi Hulk
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>Constructed at the southern end of the Orkney system, Fort Albi was a small waystation for Gallic shipments and patrols being sent to the Bretonian front through the Hebrides and Taus. Additional modules were installed throughout the Gallic War to fortify the station against threats pouring from the Tau region.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>With the end of the Gallic War, Fort Albi became a reinforced border station, providing much needed vigil from the lawless Taus. Although, recently the Gallic Union had repurposed the station to instead serve as a Bounty Hunters Guild headquarters in Gallia, deeming their potential to be more fruitful at her borders, rather than the heartlands.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>The base would be abandoned following the appearance of Nomads within Orkney in addition to the cessation of trade flowing through the system.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Cordes Wreck
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>CLASS: Liberte</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>GRAVITY: None</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>DOCKING: No</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>AMENITIES: No</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>CREW: 0</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>Originally constructed by The Council in 817 AS, Cordes began its service as Reunion Station. Following a decisive but short-lived victory in Languedoc, The Council breached the Montpellier Minefield and cleared a path into Orkney. The base was hastily assembled with aid from the first Sirians The Council encountered - the IMG. As The Council broadcast their existence to Sirius alongside dire warnings of the Gallic Crown's intentions, the station became the symbol of Sirius' very literal reunion with a seemingly lost Alliance nation, after seven centuries of seclusion.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>The Council's warning to Bretonia and Liberty forced King Charles of Gallia to launch the invasion of Sirius immediately. By 818 AS, Languedoc had fallen entirely under Crown control, with Reunion captured soon after. Renamed to Cordes Outpost, the Gallic Royal Navy put the station to use as a logistics platform, supporting the fleet that was pouring through the Westray into Tau-23. This role continued until a permanent Jump Gate was constructed between Languedoc and Tau-23 in 821 AS. Then deemed redundant for supply purposes, the station fell into obscurity as little more than a Gallic Royal Intelligence listening post.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>Despite -- or perhaps because -- of this, Cordes was one of the first installations to pledge loyalty to the Royal Enclave in 826 AS. After receiving reinforcements from the Battleship Montmorency, Cordes was fortified as a bulwark against Confederal Gallia and a launching point for raids into Gallic core space. This came to an end in late 827 AS with the incorporation of the Enclave into the Gallic Union. As a sign of good faith during negotiations with the then-Confederacy, Enclave leaders agreed to scuttle Cordes as a symbolic laying down of arms</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Vierzon Wreck
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>While Planet Eday was found by the IMG to be an unremarkable cold lifeless planet, its gravity well attracts micrometeors that orbit around the Orkney main star. The micrometeor dust field is almost impossible to notice with the naked eye, but a more extensive study proved said micrometeors to be rich in precious metals, materials rarely encountered in large quantities in Gallia.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>Finding this trove was one thing, mining it was another. It took the Gallic Metal Service some time to come up with a reliable way to capture and process the rapid meteors, and used the natural gravity well of Lannion to harness them. Once successful field tests had been carried out, Vierzon was completed to maintain the small mining fleet of specialized craft that work the field and process the various metals.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>In the disarray of the war's conclusion, GMS abandoned Vierzon. Despite this, the Enclave quickly secured the station and resumed mining. Following the incorporation of the Enclave into the new Gallic Union, Vierzon was returned to GMS control. The return to GMS ownership would not last long however, as Orkney suffered as a result of Vagrant migration from the Omicrons, ultimately resulting in the destruction of the facility along with others in the System.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Sprague Docking Ring

objects.name: Aland Wreck
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>Aland Shipyard was a former IMG installation tooled to produce and maintain a wide variety of mining ships in the region. At the height of the Gallic war, its potential to serve as the provider of emergency repairs for the drydock deprived Bretonian Kingdom came under scrutiny. And after a series of botched negotiations, tensions escalated and the shipyard was forcibly occupied for the remainder of the war. Placed under BMM's charge as the seemingly pertinent industrial authority, the station remained in Bretonian hands post-war, intended to be auctioned off to a favorably inclined third party. </TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>These plans would neither be finalized nor come to fruition as the shipyard would be struck by the worst incident of sabotage to date. Station overrides were engaged to run the reactor at emergency output, while also sealing the towers responsible for venting the pungent byproduct. The resulting systems failure made it impossible to rectify before the effects became station-wide, at which point an explosive device was triggered. As a result of its direct impact being coupled with the pervasive amount of toxic smog, the explosion ripped much of the shipyard inside out during operational hours, producing a substantial death toll of hundreds. </TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>The damage is so thorough and extensive that there is little utility to any considerations of repair or reactivation. Though BMM has not yet made any move to comment on the incident, the Mollys have passionately taken credit for the destruction of this formerly independent asset.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Omega-7 -> Omega-3
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>A jump gate is a conveyance technology that allows instantaneous travel between two distinct points in space using technology pioneered by Ageira Technologies and built by Deep Space Engineering in 130 AS. objects.name: Omega-11 Jump Hole
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TRA data="65281" mask="-31" def="30"/><TEXT>***GRAVITATIONAL ANOMALY DETECTED***</TEXT><PARA/><TRA data="96" mask="-31" def="-1"/><TEXT> </TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>Magnetic and gravimetric readings are consistent with a Jump Hole -- a natural phenomenon that functions similar to a Jump Gate, though the hazards associated with traveling through a Jump Hole remain largely unknown. Like Jump Gates, jump holes are semi-permeable areas in real-space that have a tendency to breach the natural boundaries of linear time and space. Unlike Jump Gates, though, these anomalies occur naturally and so are both unpredictable and unstable. Traveling through jump holes is a risky proposition at best. Though some have been charted and, based on accounts from ships that have accidentally encountered them, have had their exit points logged, just as many ships have never been heard from again. It is believed that these ships were either crushed in the violent, cataclysmic vortex that lies outside the narrow corridor of a jump tunnel, or were sent to a place far enough away to make communication or a return trip infeasible. In either case, those missing are presumed dead. Ageira Technologies and Deep Space Engineering urge all citizens to use the prescribed Trade Lanes and Jump Gates and to avoid all contact with jump holes.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Planet Schutz
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>DIAMETER: 4,972 km</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>MASS: 3.0 x 10e24 kg</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>TERRAIN: Volcanic</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>TEMPERATURE: 300°C to 500°C</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>ESCAPE VELOCITY: 6.75 km/sec</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT> </TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>Named after the senior lieutenant on Von Rohe's fateful expedition, Schutz is a dying planet, slowly being melted by the swelling red giant sun at the system's center. One of only two planets still intact in the system, its surface is convulsed by numerous volcanos. It serves as a shield for the Solarius station, protecting it from the intense radiation emitted by the dying sun.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Planet Deidus
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>DIAMETER: 8,972 km</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>MASS: 4.78 x 10e24 kg</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>TERRAIN: Desert</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>TEMPERATURE: -70°C to 50°C</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>ESCAPE VELOCITY: 9.75 km/sec</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT> </TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>Despite possessing a thin atmosphere, this planetoid is rendered uninhabitable by the choking, acrid dust that covers its surface -- in some places to a depth of several kilometers. objects.name: Honshu Jump Hole
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TRA data="65281" mask="-31" def="30"/><TEXT>***GRAVITATIONAL ANOMALY DETECTED***</TEXT><PARA/><TRA data="96" mask="-31" def="-1"/><TEXT> </TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>Magnetic and gravimetric readings are consistent with a Jump Hole -- a natural phenomenon that functions similar to a Jump Gate, though the hazards associated with traveling through a Jump Hole remain largely unknown. Like Jump Gates, jump holes are semi-permeable areas in real-space that have a tendency to breach the natural boundaries of linear time and space. Unlike Jump Gates, though, these anomalies occur naturally and so are both unpredictable and unstable. Traveling through jump holes is a risky proposition at best. Though some have been charted and, based on accounts from ships that have accidentally encountered them, have had their exit points logged, just as many ships have never been heard from again. It is believed that these ships were either crushed in the violent, cataclysmic vortex that lies outside the narrow corridor of a jump tunnel, or were sent to a place far enough away to make communication or a return trip infeasible. In either case, those missing are presumed dead. Ageira Technologies and Deep Space Engineering urge all citizens to use the prescribed Trade Lanes and Jump Gates and to avoid all contact with jump holes.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Kurile Docking Ring
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TRA data="65281" mask="-31" def="30"/><TEXT>>>>WARNING: Do not attempt planetary landing without using a Docking Ring.<<<</TEXT><PARA/><TRA data="96" mask="-31" def="-1"/><TEXT> </TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>A docking ring is a piece of orbiting technology that, through the use of super strong crystalline polymers and frictionless bearings, assists the smooth atmospheric entry of any interstellar vessel that has the ability to land. Invented in 130 AS by Ageira Technologies, these 'orbital elevators' almost completely negate the cost of boosting people or materials out of a planetary gravity well. Docking rings revolutionized exploration and industry almost overnight, opening up entire systems for commercial exploration and exploitation.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>Ageira Technologies licenses this technology to the other houses, who in turn agree to design all ships (except for special exploratory and survey vessels), to work with the docking ring system.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Veracruz Network
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>This network of satellites was deployed by Deep Space Engineering around Planet Veracruz in 830 AS. Designed to monitor for intruders or technological signs on the planet's surface, the network functions as a dead man's hand, beaming FTL updates back to Liberty. A significant network outage will provoke an investigation by the Liberty Navy, leading most local forces to ignore the satellites as an annoying cost of business. Onboard transponders declare that interference with the network is a criminal offense that may be punished with lethal force.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Tau-23 Jump Hole
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TRA data="65281" mask="-31" def="30"/><TEXT>***GRAVITATIONAL ANOMALY DETECTED***</TEXT><PARA/><TRA data="96" mask="-31" def="-1"/><TEXT> </TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>Magnetic and gravimetric readings are consistent with a Jump Hole -- a natural phenomenon that functions similar to a Jump Gate, though the hazards associated with traveling through a Jump Hole remain largely unknown. Like Jump Gates, jump holes are semi-permeable areas in real-space that have a tendency to breach the natural boundaries of linear time and space. Unlike Jump Gates, though, these anomalies occur naturally and so are both unpredictable and unstable. Traveling through jump holes is a risky proposition at best. Though some have been charted and, based on accounts from ships that have accidentally encountered them, have had their exit points logged, just as many ships have never been heard from again. It is believed that these ships were either crushed in the violent, cataclysmic vortex that lies outside the narrow corridor of a jump tunnel, or were sent to a place far enough away to make communication or a return trip infeasible. In either case, those missing are presumed dead. Ageira Technologies and Deep Space Engineering urge all citizens to use the prescribed Trade Lanes and Jump Gates and to avoid all contact with jump holes.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Freeport 6 Auction Office
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TRA data="1" mask="1" def="-2"/><JUST loc="center"/><TEXT>Freeport 6 Auction Office "Day 6"</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TRA data="0" mask="1" def="-1"/><JUST loc="left"/><TEXT>With Freeport 6 generally enjoying high popularity both among visitors as well as the regional factions, including the House of Kusari, it was only a matter of time until a clever entrepreneur would use the opportunity at hand and establish and provide a moderated location for used ships to change their owners legally. As a result, Mirjam "Gold Hand" Krasinski convinced enough investors to fund the construction of the Freeport 6 Auction Office, an extension of Freeport 6 that is all about trading and auctioning vessels from all over Sirius.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>The construction of the extension ended in 834 AS and was celebrated widely among ship vendors, who finally have a legal and unified marketplace. Even with rather strict limitations on what types of ships may be auctioned and traded, many regional parties are strongly interested in the ever changing offers and auctions.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>The public attention and frequent inspections of faction representatives who wish to ensure that their technologies don't end up in the wrong hands leave little wiggle room for more exotic trade opportunities. Nevertheless, with Freeport 6 and the Taus being rather crowded and full of hidden locations, it might just be impossible to fully prevent black market ship auctions.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Harris Docking Ring
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TRA data="65281" mask="-31" def="30"/><TEXT>>>>WARNING: Do not attempt planetary landing without using a Docking Ring.<<<</TEXT><PARA/><TRA data="96" mask="-31" def="-1"/><TEXT> </TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>A docking ring is a piece of orbiting technology that, through the use of super strong crystalline polymers and frictionless bearings, assists the smooth atmospheric entry of any interstellar vessel that has the ability to land. Invented in 130 AS by Ageira Technologies, these 'orbital elevators' almost completely negate the cost of boosting people or materials out of a planetary gravity well. Docking rings revolutionized exploration and industry almost overnight, opening up entire systems for commercial exploration and exploitation.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>Ageira Technologies licenses this technology to the other houses, who in turn agree to design all ships (except for special exploratory and survey vessels), to work with the docking ring system.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TRA data="65281" mask="-31" def="30"/><TEXT>***GRAVITATIONAL ANOMALY DETECTED***</TEXT><PARA/><TRA data="96" mask="-31" def="-1"/><TEXT> </TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>Magnetic and gravimetric readings are consistent with a Jump Hole -- a natural phenomenon that functions similar to a Jump Gate, though the hazards associated with traveling through a Jump Hole remain largely unknown. Like Jump Gates, jump holes are semi-permeable areas in real-space that have a tendency to breach the natural boundaries of linear time and space. Unlike Jump Gates, though, these anomalies occur naturally and so are both unpredictable and unstable. Traveling through jump holes is a risky proposition at best. Though some have been charted and, based on accounts from ships that have accidentally encountered them, have had their exit points logged, just as many ships have never been heard from again. It is believed that these ships were either crushed in the violent, cataclysmic vortex that lies outside the narrow corridor of a jump tunnel, or were sent to a place far enough away to make communication or a return trip infeasible. In either case, those missing are presumed dead. Ageira Technologies and Deep Space Engineering urge all citizens to use the prescribed Trade Lanes and Jump Gates and to avoid all contact with jump holes.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Planet Rugen
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>DIAMETER: 9,145 km.</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>MASS: 5.05 x 10e24 kg.</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>TERRAIN: Desert</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>TEMPERATURE: 18°C to 92°C</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>ESCAPE VELOCITY: 9.1 km/sec</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT> </TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>A sterile desert world, Rugen provides a bleak backdrop to Bornholm Station and its notorious Pit arena. Limited surveys indicate the planet may possess Silver and Cobalt deposits, however local Junkers are usually quick to run off any would-be pioneers who could bring unwanted attention to their operations. It is alleged that the Junkers will dump trespassers or overly unruly guests among Rugen's dunes to wander until they inevitably suffocate. Rugen has accumulated a debris field in orbit, however it is unclear to what extent this stems from the Junker's activities, or alleged Rheinland experiments from the late 790s. Showers of scrap burning up in the atmosphere frequently light Rugen's night sky.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>You'd think an assignment like this would suck. None of the creature comforts of Mactan or Cochrane here, no sir. I can live with that though, because Barrier Gate is a hop and a skip away. Now that place is a real oasis in the desert. Whenever I have downtime, my Bayonet is straight out the hangar and off to the casinos.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>The crew of the Insidious are a weird mix. Some of us were forced to put a pin in our lavish lifestyles to repay favors or clear debts. Others are the freaky "true believer" sort, who're here to play as super-cool subversives, sticking it to The Man. They can die for a cause if they want, but it's not for me. I'm living forever.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>The LSF couldn't lock down Jericho quick enough to keep the news under wraps. Hard to hide an entire Trade Lane project getting wiped out, not to mention the rolling blackouts on Yuma. Alien ruins are in vogue now, the hot stuff of Los Angeles gossip over synth-lattes. The people want info, and luckily enough, we're on site and happy to oblige... for a price.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>I had to sign on with the Insidious to clear a debt with one of the Executives on Cochrane. I got in over my head on a Cardamine tab, bartered my skills as a signals analyst to get out of the hole. Now I'm stuck here, and missing out on pulling apart a damn Jump Drive.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Prison Liner Helsingborg
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>The IMG base is somewhere in the Malvinas Cloud. That's the area I'm supposed to hang out in when I'm not here refitting and refueling. I don't envy those miners. If the Outcasts figure out where the base is, there are going to be lots of dead miners floating around. </TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>The Insidious has the largest open bounty in Liberty, higher than even the Gatebreakers who ran off with the Niyodo core. The LSF were pretty steamed that we managed to sneak into Alaska a few years back, and leak some juicy scans of Juneau Shipyard. At the time, Liberty's official position was that Alaska didn't exist.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>Crayter rescued a bunch of ex-slaves from the Taus, and has been parading them around on Yuma. We went sniffing through their identities and found most of them are Insurgency war prisoners who the LPI trafficked from the camps on Planet Erie. Crayter doesn't know what they've got, and we'll be sure to let the public know when the time is right. Major incident in the making!</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TRA data="65281" mask="-31" def="30"/><TEXT>>>>WARNING: NAVIGATION HAZARD<<<</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TRA data="96" mask="-31" def="-1"/><TEXT>The Isere Debris Field was created during the Battles of Montpellier in 733 AGS and 734 AGS (817 - 818 AS), during the Second Gallic Civil War. This conflict between the Council and Gallic Royal Navy resulted in the breaching of the Montpellier Minefield, and the Council’s Languedoc fleet escaping into Sirius. The battlefield’s wreckage is often scavenged by Gallic Brigands.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>
Santa Clara
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>The Santa Clara was the personal fighter of notorious Coalition commissar Sophia Wirtz. Her ship was destroyed in 830 AS, with the hull being scored by impacts consistent with both Coalition tachyon and Core particle weapons.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>This Valkyrie's serial codes match with declassified Rheinland records indicating it was assigned to the Battleship Verthandi. The battleship and its squadrons were listed as lost in 800 AS. It is unclear how the Aggressor came to be located in The Barrier.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>
objects.infocard: Tourmenteur-3

objects.name: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>Crayter has sealed military records about a major battle that happened in 827 AS, somewhere nearby. We haven't been able to get into the file yet. It's a fair bet it's related to the ruins and wreckage we detected while traveling here from Cortez. I'd recommend you keep your distance, there's all sorts of weird readings.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>
objects.infocard: Aggressor-6

objects.name: Hoedspruit
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>The Core destroyer Hoedspruit was constructed at Alabama Shipyard in 829 AS. Dispatched to Dagger Outpost to serve in the local defense force, it later participated in the assault on Kamchatka Station alongside its sister ship Letaba. While patrolling in early 835 AS, it encountered a large swarm of AI Drones. The Hoedspruit was quickly overwhelmed and torn apart; no survivors or bodies were found at the wreck.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Kamchatka Wreck
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>CLASS: Petersburg</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>Gravity: No</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>Docking: No</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>Amenities: No</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>Crew: 0</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>Kamchatka Base was constructed by the Coalition in 820 AS, hidden deep within the Kattegat Lava Field. The Coalition and their Red Hessian allies had been deeply shocked by the Second Casablanca Offensive, as the Corsair assault from Omega-55 had exposed a severe vulnerability in their flanks. The installation was strategically situated to monitor traffic headed to or from Omega-47, with orders to sever Corsair supply lines while protecting the Coalition's own convoys to Omega-11. Kamchatka was a bloody and swelteringly hot posting that was deeply unpopular with serving crews; despite this, Coalition commanders believed the costs were justified by the security buffer created for  Omega-52.</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT></TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>Kamchatka's garrison were routinely ordered to attack difficult targets across Omega-55, despite being haphazardly equipped with the leftovers of priority squadrons in Omega-5, 47 and 52. As a result, pilot casualties were high and morale low, with many coming to see their commanders on Volgograd as ignorant of their circumstances, or maliciously incompetent. The garrison's failure to make significant headway against either the Corsairs or Core eventually led to suspicions that Kamchatka may be "politically unreliable", or even harboring "counter-revolutionary saboteurs". As a result, the station commandant was dismissed in 826 AS, and a cadre of political officers dispatched to enforce party loyalty and revolutionary fervor with an iron fist.</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT></TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>Matters came to a head in 830 AS, when the Core battleship Bellona was sighted moored at Dagger Outpost. Kamchatka's squadrons were commanded to destroy the target; when Lieutenant Zacarías Riojas objected to the practicality of the order, he was promptly executed for insubordination. This triggered a mutiny as a decade of resentment boiled up. In the chaos, several pilots fled in an attempt to escape The Coalition and surrender to the Bellona. Now aware of the disarray at Kamchatka, The Core quickly launched their own assault, offering an amnesty to any dissidents taking up arms against their former officers. The battle was brief, with the station destroyed and loyalist Coalition forces scattered towards Omega-47.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>Ammo and equipment isn't so much of a problem on an industrial planet. We can use the factories we still hold to manufacture more. The problem is with the more basic supplies. Consumer Goods used to be ordered in from London, and we were entirely reliant on Cambridge Food Rations. With the seige in place, we've got finite stockpiles that we're having to ration carefully. Once they're gone, things get... interesting. Hopefully the engineers will have some biopods up by then so we can grow stuff here. Much like on spacestations, if you recycle everything, the only thing you need is energy, and that's something we can manage on Leeds. </TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>A Royal Enclave base, Rodez was a small, modular station that took after appraisal and scavenging of formerly Council-owned Perpignan. It was little more than a cluster of hangar modules.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>Patrols from Rodez made frequent sorties in an attempt to crack down upon Brigand and Maquis presence striking from the system's fields and nebulae, but little progress can be made against such guerilla warfare given the means currently availible to the Enclave in Roussillon.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>The Base would not survive the upheaval within the Enclave, and the Maquis, together with the Gaians from nearby Edinburgh destroyed the base and the Enclave within the system retreated to Orkney.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Tau-23 Jump Hole
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TRA data="65281" mask="-31" def="30"/><TEXT>***GRAVITATIONAL ANOMALY DETECTED***</TEXT><PARA/><TRA data="96" mask="-31" def="-1"/><TEXT> </TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>Magnetic and gravimetric readings are consistent with a Jump Hole -- a natural phenomenon that functions similar to a Jump Gate, though the hazards associated with traveling through a Jump Hole remain largely unknown. Like Jump Gates, jump holes are semi-permeable areas in real-space that have a tendency to breach the natural boundaries of linear time and space. Unlike Jump Gates, though, these anomalies occur naturally and so are both unpredictable and unstable. Traveling through jump holes is a risky proposition at best. Though some have been charted and, based on accounts from ships that have accidentally encountered them, have had their exit points logged, just as many ships have never been heard from again. It is believed that these ships were either crushed in the violent, cataclysmic vortex that lies outside the narrow corridor of a jump tunnel, or were sent to a place far enough away to make communication or a return trip infeasible. In either case, those missing are presumed dead. Ageira Technologies and Deep Space Engineering urge all citizens to use the prescribed Trade Lanes and Jump Gates and to avoid all contact with jump holes.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>A jump gate is a conveyance technology that allows instantaneous travel between two distinct points in space using technology pioneered by Ageira Technologies and built by Deep Space Engineering in 130 AS. objects.name: Planet Miura
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>The Flint didn't make it from Buffalo to Rochester on a routine Cardamine smuggling run several weeks ago. There was no distress call, no reports of LPI or Navy interdiction heard on comms. It probably hit an asteroid somewhere in the western quadrant of the Badlands, off of the regular patrol routes. </TEXT><PARA/><TEXT> </TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Kamakura Base
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>The Nurnberg was making a gun run from here to Omega-11 when it was attacked by a Federal Police patrol while crossing the open area in the center of the system. The ship was pursued into the Westnebel, where it lost contact. Because it never arrived in Freital, the police must have destroyed it. </TEXT><PARA/><TEXT> </TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Isehara Refinery
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>There are multiple dead ships floating in a radiation pocket of the Ruhrfeld. They are most likely Unioners, maybe a Red Hessian or two. Most of them have been stripped clean, but there may still be a few with one or two weapons left on them. </TEXT><PARA/><TEXT> </TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Miura Docking Ring
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TRA data="65281" mask="-31" def="30"/><TEXT>>>>WARNING: Do not attempt planetary landing without using a Docking Ring.<<<</TEXT><PARA/><TRA data="96" mask="-31" def="-1"/><TEXT> </TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>A docking ring is a piece of orbiting technology that, through the use of super strong crystalline polymers and frictionless bearings, assists the smooth atmospheric entry of any interstellar vessel that has the ability to land. Invented in 130 AS by Ageira Technologies, these 'orbital elevators' almost completely negate the cost of boosting people or materials out of a planetary gravity well. Docking rings revolutionized exploration and industry almost overnight, opening up entire systems for commercial exploration and exploitation.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>Ageira Technologies licenses this technology to the other houses, who in turn agree to design all ships (except for special exploratory and survey vessels), to work with the docking ring system.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>Ammo and equipment isn't so much of a problem on an industrial planet. We can use the factories we still hold to manufacture more. The problem is with the more basic supplies. Consumer Goods used to be ordered in from London, and we were entirely reliant on Cambridge Food Rations. With the seige in place, we've got finite stockpiles that we're having to ration carefully. Once they're gone, things get... interesting. Hopefully the engineers will have some biopods up by then so we can grow stuff here. Much like on spacestations, if you recycle everything, the only thing you need is energy, and that's something we can manage on Leeds. </TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Barossa
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>The Barossa was an Independent Miners Guild freighter attempting to transport Niobium out of Tau-37. The ship was attacked by Outcasts. While an IMG patrol managed to chase off the Outcasts, with its crew dead and engines damaged, the freighter drifted off into the cloud and was lost.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Barberry
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>A Cryer Pharmaceuticals escort fighter, piloted by Jake Thompson. Nearly every external component of Barberry is damaged or missing.</TEXT><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Griffin
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>The Griffin was a Bounty Hunter Vessel that was lost after the pilot, Jessica Stephenson, chased some Outcasts into the Bermejo Cloud. According to the Bounty Hunter's Guild, Jessica was known to have close ties with APM, the developers of the Bounty Hunter's shiplines.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>Given her history, it is unknown why she would have been so far out in the Edgeworlds, especially as she had not accepted any bounty request at the time.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Il Fiocina
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>Most of the ship's cruise disruptor supply has been expended. System logs indicate outbound transmissions requesting backup. The hull bears the scorch marks of transport-class turrets, and the shield generator has been rendered inoperable.</TEXT><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Achlidon
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>The communication logs in the black box recorder show navigation requests from IMG ships.</TEXT><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Thorax
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>The communication logs in the black box recorder show navigation requests from IMG ships.</TEXT><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Antares
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>Antares bears no cargo manifests in its computer system, but its recording devices indicate it was last moored on Malta's surface. The telltale blisters of particle blasts spot its hull, and its engines and life support systems are completely destroyed.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>The bodies aboard, though bloated and desiccated by vacuum exposure, distinctly seem to lack Outcast uniforms.</TEXT><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Siren
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>Freeport 10's launch records list Siren's last launch as a search and rescue mission. objects.name: Omicron Alpha Jump Hole
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TRA data="65281" mask="-31" def="30"/><TEXT>***GRAVITATIONAL ANOMALY DETECTED***</TEXT><PARA/><TRA data="96" mask="-31" def="-1"/><TEXT> </TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>Magnetic and gravimetric readings are consistent with a Jump Hole -- a natural phenomenon that functions similar to a Jump Gate, though the hazards associated with traveling through a Jump Hole remain largely unknown. Like Jump Gates, jump holes are semi-permeable areas in real-space that have a tendency to breach the natural boundaries of linear time and space. Unlike Jump Gates, though, these anomalies occur naturally and so are both unpredictable and unstable. Traveling through jump holes is a risky proposition at best. Though some have been charted and, based on accounts from ships that have accidentally encountered them, have had their exit points logged, just as many ships have never been heard from again. It is believed that these ships were either crushed in the violent, cataclysmic vortex that lies outside the narrow corridor of a jump tunnel, or were sent to a place far enough away to make communication or a return trip infeasible. In either case, those missing are presumed dead. Ageira Technologies and Deep Space Engineering urge all citizens to use the prescribed Trade Lanes and Jump Gates and to avoid all contact with jump holes.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Pathfinder
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>The wreck of the Pathfinder is all that remains of the famous Bounty Hunter T. "Bob" Biggs's last voyage.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>Sharing an eerily similar story as other pilots in search of fortune through pillaging and assassinating Outcast ships, Biggs followed this course of action after finishing his sentence aboard the LPI Prison Ship Sugarland. He rose through the ranks of the Guild at a rapid pace, and acquired significant wealth from hunting down Liberty Rogues and Xenos. However, still desiring for more, he set off to Tau-37, from which he launched frequent raids into Outcast space, going as far as the other regions of the Omicron Alpha system and even entering into the nearby ones.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>One day, the patrols finally caught up with his ship on the outskirts of Omicron Alpha, close to the Beta Jump Hole. He was promptly shot down, with the Pathfinder towed to Omicron Beta, acting as a reminder to Bounty Hunters and other intruders alike of the dangers posed by entering such areas.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Hosho Maru
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>Launched in 786 AS, the Hosho Maru was a top-of-the-line GMG vessel equipped for surveying gas fields for resources. With the Sigma-13 gas mining slowing down, it embarked upon a journey of discovering new fields for the GMG to exploit.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>This took it to the outskirts of the Sigmas, whereupon it entered a new Jump Hole previously uncharted. The thirst for curiosity was the crew's downfall, however, as they did not spend much time in the Omicron Beta before being located and captured by the Outcasts.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>No signs of the crew have ever been returned, but the wreck of the Hosho Maru remains as intact as it has been at launch, still containing many of the materials used for its mission.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

Unlike Jump Gates, though, these anomalies occur naturally and so are both unpredictable and unstable. Traveling through jump holes is a risky proposition at best. Though some have been charted and, based on accounts from ships that have accidentally encountered them, have had their exit points logged, just as many ships have never been heard from again. It is believed that these ships were either crushed in the violent, cataclysmic vortex that lies outside the narrow corridor of a jump tunnel, or were sent to a place far enough away to make communication or a return trip infeasible. In either case, those missing are presumed dead. Ageira Technologies and Deep Space Engineering urge all citizens to use the prescribed Trade Lanes and Jump Gates and to avoid all contact with jump holes.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>
