objects.name: Fes Wreck
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>The Battleship Fes was a heavily modified Osiris-class vessel that was commissioned at Tripoli Shipyard in 809 AS. As the prototype Corsair battleship, the Fes spent its initial years patrolling Omicron Gamma, before being deployed to the Hessian fronts of Omega 5 and 48. It would spend the next decade and a half embroiled in these stalemates, gradually becoming more outdated and outclassed as time went on. When the Corsairs sent a fleet to assist in the Gallic invasion of New London in 826 AS, the Elders felt the venerable Fes would be a liability on the front line. Instead it was redeployed to Cambridge and tasked with targeting Bretonian shipping.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>With the Corsairs' New London fleet routed soon after, the Fes withdrew for refitting, emerging once more in Omega-47 several months later. The Fes launched a probing attack on Planet Tangier, finding unexpected success when it was revealed that much of the garrison had been sent to reinforce Hessian activities in Cologne and Dresden. Viernheim Base was quickly destroyed, with the operation on Planet Tangier being saved only by the intervention of the Coalition carrier Alvin Katz. The two warships inflicted heavy damage on one another, with the Fes ultimately retreating back to Omega 5.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>Upon reaching Tripoli Shipyard, a full damage assessment indicated that the Fes would be prohibitively expensive to fully repair, especially when more advanced generations of warships had left it largely obsolete. The Fes languished for several years before receiving basic patch repairs and being deployed to Omicron Theta as a guard ship. In 832 AS, the Fes would be caught by an Outcast strike group led by the Battlecruiser Augusta while maneuvering near the Orinoco Cloud. The battleship stood little chance against these modern vessels, but succeeded in raising the alarm and dispatching the Destroyer Bella and several Outcast strike wings during its last stand.</TEXT><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Destroyer Bella
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>Outcast Destroyers are built with attack in mind, with speed and agility being prioritised to make best use of the Outcasts' piloting skills. The Bella was commissioned in 822 AS as part of a destroyer hunting pack assigned to the Dreadnought Basilica. In this capacity, it would carry out several tours of the Taus, participating with distinction in the 827 AS offensive against the Crayter Republic. The Bella would later accompany the Basilica to its new posting in Omicron Theta, where it was primarily responsible for hunting down Corsair Artifact smugglers.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>Bella's pack would be prematurely withdrawn to Omicron Alpha with the Basilica because of the Maltese Slave Revolt. Following the Revolt's defeat, the Bella was reassigned to the Battlecruiser Augusta to provide local experience for its posting to Omicron Theta. The strike force was instructed to undermine the Corsairs in the system, and to destroy Freeport 9's biodomes if possible. Early in their deployment, the group caught the venerable Battleship Fes on patrol near the Orinoco Cloud.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>While the relatively new and advanced Outcast ships significantly outclassed the Fes, the Bella would take critical damage during a recklessly close run on the Corsair battleship's engines. The Fes would be dispatched by the Augusta, while the Bella's surviving crew scuttled the destroyer to prevent Corsair reinforcements from capturing it. The two wrecks now drift through the Theta warzone side by side.</TEXT><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>Ammo and equipment isn't so much of a problem on an industrial planet. We can use the factories we still hold to manufacture more. The problem is with the more basic supplies. Consumer Goods used to be ordered in from London, and we were entirely reliant on Cambridge Food Rations. With the seige in place, we've got finite stockpiles that we're having to ration carefully. Once they're gone, things get... interesting. Hopefully the engineers will have some biopods up by then so we can grow stuff here. Much like on spacestations, if you recycle everything, the only thing you need is energy, and that's something we can manage on Leeds. </TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Mooring Fixture
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>A mooring fixture is a temporary resting area for idle ships within active shipping zones, allowing transports and other large vessels to be unloaded and passengers transferred.  </TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: PSI-N0K
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>The fast and unremitting precision of the Cruisers lurking in the vicinity of Gammu during the final offensive orchestrated by the Mars were the very reason behind the top Core battle analysts and strategists believing that deploying a mass-scale offensive towards their frigid home in such a small window of time would likely result in a dismal and pyrrhic victory. But against every possible odd, the Core forces buckled the defensive perimeter composed of Gammu Cruiser assault packs and the Carrier Orion deployed by the Technocracy through sheer aggression with only minimal losses, resulting in the Gammu’s subsequent and questionably quick retreat as the Core quickly established dominance over the entire perimeter of the planet.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>A quick data analysis within the almost oceanic pool of data stored inside the data banks profiles displays multiple baffling directives followed by the large automation flawlessly. Such directives consisted in investigating and archiving nearby asteroid and debris activity, registering the radioactive emissions unleashed by the raging radioactive sun of Omicron Kappa, as well as relaying the trajectory of tantalized and foolhardy pilots who were bold enough to enter the vicinity of Gammu’s orbit. </TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>There are several thousands of other such entries within the navigational archives, repeating themselves in precise and unerring patterns for entire decades, until one particular directive tasked the machine with repelling the incoming Core assault team advancing towards Gammu's orbit. In adherence with the glaring reported damage visible to the naked eye sustained by ballistic and concentrated high energy fire, this vessel retreated in the far distance away from the losing battle, prioritizing its own escape according to the ubiquitous directives dispensed from Gammu prior to their catastrophic fall by the hands of their aggressors.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>Now, the thing from the stars rests in an empty asteroid. Inert, battered and broken, the impossible wiring tangled into impossible shapes still floating aimlessly in the emptiness of space.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>The machine’s final set destination is towards home.</TEXT><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Frosty
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>This Gammu Cruiser appears to be fully shut down. A thin layer of crystaline material covers the hull. Due to the system-wide radiation, standard scanners are unable to analyze the exact structural composition. Livadia's published drone research registry lists this cruiser as "Frosty" - with a note regarding this unit's extraordinary behavior.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>"Frosty, Gammu AI Harvester, registered entity #215 - nickname given by Alexander Winslow. While attempts to communicate Gammu AI units, especially cruiser-sized ones, has always been rather difficult, it was not with this one. I was talking with Tim about something trivial while observing this cruiser from close proximity. It seemed to be in a passive state."</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>"At the end of the conversation, Tim said 'Stay frosty!' while the comms must have been active. As immediate response, the cruiser reacted by repeating the recorded voice line over and over again - 'Frosty'. We are yet to figure out why it did it, but the reaction resulted in this nickname for 215."</TEXT><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Peeper
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>This Gammu Drone appears to be fully shut down. A thin layer of crystaline material covers the hull. Due to the system-wide radiation, standard scanners are unable to analyze the exact structural composition. Livadia's published drone research registry lists this drone as "Peeper" - with a note regarding this drone's particularly nosy yet pacifistic nature.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>"Peeper, Gammu AI Drone, registered entity #378 - nickname given by Alexander Winslow. We marked Peeper with a photon-based tattoo after getting its permission. We are not sure why Peeper agreed to the procedure without any question. We assume Peeper finds merit in the idea of being easily distinguishable from other, otherwise pristine AI drones. Peeper seems to avoid conflict at all cost and generally flees from any non-livadian vessel. In fact, Peeper allows any liviadian asset to get close, yet not closer than 27.315 feet. No, Shane, I do not know what that is in meters."</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>The livadian drone research registry does not mention Shane at any other point. </TEXT><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Skoot
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>This Gammu Drone appears to be fully shut down. A thin layer of crystaline material covers the hull. Due to the system-wide radiation, standard scanners are unable to analyze the exact structural composition. Livadia's published drone research registry lists this drone as "Skoot" - with a note.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>"Skoot, Gammu AI Drone, registered entity #304 - nickname given by Alexander Winslow. Named this one after Vanessa's gaian ground sloth - because it might just be the laziest drone I have been watching. Skoot is easily identified because of its incredibly weak energy signature, possibly as a result of a damaged component. This drone seems to avoid the proximity of other drones. I wonder if it is afraid of getting replaced. Need to look into that, after the date with Vanessa."</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: CHI-70P
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>These are the unmistakable remains of a Gammu drone dispatched from the frigid surface of Gammu. The scarred hull, once composed of various complex alloys stretched and re-arranged into unrecognizable and mystifying patterns, appears to have been sundered apart by relentless plasma cannons, leaving nothing but a dead vessel behind, its technological innards still floating in the hollow vacuum of space.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>The complete absence of any recognizable navigational hardware or data memory banks suggest that this particular vessel was shot down, and later divested and desecrated from the more valuable parts by an unknown party.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: ETA-B3E
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>Scanner and data profiling confirms that this inert vessel is another drone sent the elusive Gammu, hailing from their eponymous planet. The sheer distance travelled by this particular drone combined with a basic carbonic analysis suggests that this particular drone was deployed for space reconnaissance decades ago, as the puzzling on-board reactor appears to have already seen a lot of mileage.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>Any navigational data extracted from this wrecked machine only confirms the baffling protocols and algorithms followed by the Gammu, as the vessel seems to have travelled the entire solar system in an elliptical pattern repeatedly several thousands of times, before finally breaking apart and finding refuge in a large, hollow asteroid in a remote periphery within the system. </TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>The latest encrypted and undecipherable transmissions sent by this machine back to the subnet relays of Gammu were met with no response.</TEXT><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Core Fighter
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>With structural failure, a shattered hull, and other signs of damage, this ship bears the scars of battle, never to be healed.</TEXT><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Badmouth
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>A heavily damaged lone Core Requiem rests inside this hollow asteroid. According to the on-board data, it belonged to fighter pilot Oliver "Badmouth" Emerson. The inside of the cockpit appears to be still pressurised, while the late pilot has been presumably retrieved by his cohorts. The composition of the cabin appears to be mostly composed of carbon dioxide, making the fate of the pilot inside uncertain.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>The Requiem presents severe lesions and dire wounds inflicted by several laser cuts, some of which severely impacted and knocked out the main reactor, leaving the reckless pilot stranded, alone and unable to contact anyone. </TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>According to the mission logs, Badmouth was part of the strike wing of fighters who laid waste to the ground defenses through the employment of explosive ordinance. The pilot, in his hubris, disregarded a direct order to not give chase to any fleeing Gammu drones. The pilot continued to open fire at the remaining automations, before being ultimately cornered by them as they fought back, leaving his disabled ship out to drift into a nearby asteroid.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>The disabled ship's final log recordings are appended within the blackbox.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>"To anyone who can read this: this is Badmouth. I thought I could show those Gammu tangos who's boss. They were just a bunch of glorified toasters who never stood a chance against us... until I tried to chase them down by myself. I tried telling my CO that I have been scrapping these things for a while now, but as it turns out, a cornered animal really knows how to put up a fight... They've messed me up good. Life support's offline, comms are offline, my engine's gone bust. I can still see Gammu from all the way out here... the lights and the explosions and the works, and I'm stranded here to sit and watch, and breathe my own air until I'll die. I'm leaving this homing beacon online until somebody finds me."</TEXT><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Timothy Avarice
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>The remains of the Core fighter "Timothy Avarice", named by his pilot of the same name. Avarice was known among the crew of Battleship Mars as youngster who desperately tried to convince people to name things after him. Due to the constant refusals of this request, Avarice simply christened his ship with his name.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>During the fight over Gammu, Avarice was listed as MIA - resulting in his wing getting renamed to "Battleship Mars - 4th Avarice Avengers".</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Khemmiset
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>DIAMETER: 4,482 km</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>MASS: 9.01 x 10e22 kg</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>TERRAIN: Rock</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>TEMPERATURE: -210°C to 180°C</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>ESCAPE VELOCITY: 2.21 km/sec</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>Khemmiset is a rocky, airless moon orbiting planet Tangier. While no comprehensive surveys have been carried out, preliminary exploration revealed deposits of Iron and silicates. There is little interest in developing the necessary infrastructure needed to mine the moon, largely due to a combination of cost, security issues, and Tangier overshadowing Khemmiset's potential.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Planet Rabat
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>DIAMETER: 50,980 km</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>MASS: 1.56 x 10e26 kg</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>TERRAIN: Rock</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>TEMPERATURE: -210°C to 180°C</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>ESCAPE VELOCITY: 28.9 km/sec</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>Planet Rabat is a relatively small gas giant that orbits the remote outskirts of Omega-47. While no commercial surveys have been conducted, cursory scans detect Hydrogen, argon, Neon and xenon in the upper atmosphere. The Corsairs initially attempted to harvest the outgassed Hydrogen and Oxygen caught in Rabat's rings, however this enterprise was abandoned with the Casablanca Offensive of 811 AS. In recent years, both Corsair and Red Hessian vessels have been sighted attempting to skim the rings for resources.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Omega-5 Jump Hole
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TRA data="65281" mask="-31" def="30"/><TEXT>***GRAVITATIONAL ANOMALY DETECTED***</TEXT><PARA/><TRA data="96" mask="-31" def="-1"/><TEXT> </TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>Magnetic and gravimetric readings are consistent with a Jump Hole -- a natural phenomenon that functions similar to a Jump Gate, though the hazards associated with traveling through a Jump Hole remain largely unknown. Like Jump Gates, jump holes are semi-permeable areas in real-space that have a tendency to breach the natural boundaries of linear time and space. Unlike Jump Gates, though, these anomalies occur naturally and so are both unpredictable and unstable. Traveling through jump holes is a risky proposition at best. Though some have been charted and, based on accounts from ships that have accidentally encountered them, have had their exit points logged, just as many ships have never been heard from again. It is believed that these ships were either crushed in the violent, cataclysmic vortex that lies outside the narrow corridor of a jump tunnel, or were sent to a place far enough away to make communication or a return trip infeasible. In either case, those missing are presumed dead. Ageira Technologies and Deep Space Engineering urge all citizens to use the prescribed Trade Lanes and Jump Gates and to avoid all contact with jump holes.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Hassani
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>The wreck of the Hassani belonged to Red Hessian ace Jakob Bautzen, whose ship was disabled during a failed raid to capture Casablanca from the Corsairs. Bautzen attempted to flee the area while being pursued by Corsair patrols. He managed to shake them in the dense El Aaiun field, but the damage to his fuel compartment was too severe.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>Stranded without fuel in the middle of nowhere, the pilot was destined for a slow death. However, the equipment appears to remain intact.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>The Order is working in close cooperation with the Independent Miners Guild to investigate and neutralize the threat at Jericho. It is our belief that we are seeing a cascading activation sequence of Daam-K’vosh facilities, likely triggered by reckless experimentation with Xeno Relics and other live Artifacts in recent years.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>Observations indicate that Jericho is leeching power directly from hyperspace, resulting in increasing phase volatility across local Jump Holes. We are unsure what this is building towards, but The Order intends to find a way to lower its shields and destroy the receiver structures.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>The Battleship Atum recently cornered the Nomad infected Battlecruiser Wyoming in Ontario. They pursued the battlecruiser through an artificial Jump Hole that had been created by alien warforms utilizing some kind of Jump Drive technology. On arriving in Vespucci, the Atum suffered heavy damage in the resulting battle. They were stranded there until local Gaians aided in a breakout to Coronado.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>The Cuyamel was forced to moor here for repairs, after she was struck by the Jericho Incident. She's a bulk freighter, and central to Universal's strategy of dominating local trade and forcing open markets. While we're out of pocket on insurance for the repairs, the contracts here are profitable enough for us to stomach the ongoing risk. If we ease off now, we give the Crayter shipping we've been squeezing room to breath.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Carrier Orion
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>CLASS: Orion</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>CREW: </TEXT><TRA data="65280" mask="-32" def="31"/><TEXT>CLASSIFIED</TEXT><PARA/><TRA data="96" mask="-32" def="-1"/><TEXT>ARMAMENT: </TEXT><TRA data="65280" mask="-32" def="31"/><TEXT>CLASSIFIED</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>This formerly BMM-owned Hegemon Asteroid Miner was recorded as lost during the fall of Graves Station and resulting secession of Dublin. The Mollys have since repurposed many of these ships for their own ends. The mining ships Hope and Fortune were withdrawn to Arranmore Base in 834 AS amid fears of an imminent Bretonian invasion of Dublin. The pair were then worked on as an "insurance policy" by Mull Base's Hellburner Squadron, and converted into enormous armored bombs.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>When Bretonia eventually attacked in 835 AS, the Hope was dispatched towards the Bretonian offensive aiming for the Achill Asteroid Field. Concealed among a screen of fellow Asteroid Miners, the Hope was heavily damaged on approach to the Battlecruiser Bracknell. Unwilling to allow the Bretonian capital ship to escape, Captain Saoirse Keane elected to forego evacuation and detonate immediately. The Bracknell's engines were crippled by this sacrifice. The immobilized ship was towed away after several days of fierce fighting.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>This Bretonia Armed Forces Fighter was lost in battle during the 835 AS Bretonian Invasion of Dublin.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Planet Fuerteventura
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>A frozen, lifeless world, Fuerteventura was surveyed by the Zoners upon their arrival in the system. Lanzarote Station was constructed in its orbit to facilitate the efficient transfer of resources and materials from the planet, aiding in the construction and colonization of Planet Gran Canaria. The most notable resource discovered was gold. While extracting it in significant quantities proved unfeasible, the amount that was mined played a role in accelerating Gran Canaria's early development.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>Unfortunately, the scarcity of easily accessible natural resources on the planet forced the Zoners to import raw materials from other systems. Over time, they shifted their reliance to resources available on Planet Gran Canaria itself. The high costs of maintaining a gold mining operation led to its eventual abandonment. Today, Fuerteventura serves as a silent companion to Lanzarote Station, which has found a new purpose: the production of the ZC-410 "Peregrine," the latest Zoner-originating frigate on the market.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Gran Canaria Atmospheric Entry Point

objects.name: Ship for sale
objects.infocard: Lares

objects.name: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>I'm going to request a transfer out of the Omegas. My acquisition debt is paid off and the contract to clear my criminal record was completed years ago. I can't do it any longer, not even for these bonuses. Every time I launch, it feels like I'm facing death. The AI raids are the final straw -- the way they fight is absolutely inhuman. I've already got my nest egg, I'd happily take a pay cut to work facility security at the Los Angeles office. I've proved my loyalty.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>The Core found me in Sugarland. I was looking down a life sentence for taking out three of the LPI patrol ships that tried to take me in. One of the Core recruiters caught wind of my story and figured my skills were wasted breaking up radioactive Scrap Metal. They offered me a contract, purchased my sentence from Liberty, and set me up with gear I could only have dreamed of as a Rogue.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>The alien ruins The Core is interested in on Skagen are deep underground. To get to them, you have to dig through "The Crunch", a thin band of skeletons and fossils we've found at a consistent depth for every bore site we've sunk. There's no signs of life before or after that band. It's like complex organisms sprung from no-where and were wiped away just as abruptly. Thinking about what happened here terrifies me.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>When you're carrying out exo-operations on Skagen, you have to wear a respirator. There's a nominally breathable atmosphere, but you'll quickly end up hypoxic from the scarce Oxygen. The geologists say there was much more Oxygen eons ago. Apparently it is slowly reacting away and will eventually dwindle to nothing. We should investigate what happened here, but Corporate's only interest is extracting Artifacts from the ruins.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Garvagh Base
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>Because we have no money or ships, we cannot patrol the Trade Lanes in Omega-7 or protect the Daumann operations in Dresden and Omega-4. The police must make do as well as they can, but that's not always sufficient when Red Hessians are involved. </TEXT><PARA/><TEXT> </TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Garvagh Hulk
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>With the Corsair advance towards Dublin becoming an increasingly alarming issue amongst the Mollys, the need for a forward base to help curb Corsair ambitions became paramount. Every step the Corsairs took in Omega-49 pressured the Mollys into taking action, resulting in their decision to construct Garvagh Base as an answer to the issue.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>Following the abandonment of Poole and the Corsair push in Dublin however, Garvagh no longer became tenable and the base was subsequently abandoned as the expenses maintaining it were better spent on the Dublin front.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>Cochrane's been fried twice by pulses from Sudbury, so we're pretty good at spotting the warning signs these days. Fool me twice, and all that. When Jericho wiped out the orbiting sensors we were piggybacking, we guessed what was happening and powered the Insidious down. Between that and The Barrier, we came through without a scratch.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>We're supposed to be baby-sitting Cardamine smugglers, but we've also got the most advanced sensors within 5 light years. With the quality of readings we could get off Jericho and the system storm, we could name our own price. I've been quietly negotiating a deal for feed data with an old Liberty University associate.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

The Alvin Katz is more than a warship. It is a testament to the courage of the Coalition's people, and proudly carries the name of a hero.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>Bowex is the primary supplier of the Bretonia Armed Forces, and unfortunately that means in times of war, we get sent to the front. It was true during the Gallic Invasion, and it's true now too. Today I was shipping H-Fuel to the Essex, which meant I didn't need to go through that horrendous Jump Hole into Dublin.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TRA data="65281" mask="-31" def="30"/><TEXT>***GRAVITATIONAL ANOMALY DETECTED***</TEXT><PARA/><TRA data="96" mask="-31" def="-1"/><TEXT> </TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>Magnetic and gravimetric readings are consistent with a Jump Hole -- a natural phenomenon that functions similar to a Jump Gate, though the hazards associated with traveling through a Jump Hole remain largely unknown. Like Jump Gates, jump holes are semi-permeable areas in real-space that have a tendency to breach the natural boundaries of linear time and space. Unlike Jump Gates, though, these anomalies occur naturally and so are both unpredictable and unstable. Traveling through jump holes is a risky proposition at best. Though some have been charted and, based on accounts from ships that have accidentally encountered them, have had their exit points logged, just as many ships have never been heard from again. It is believed that these ships were either crushed in the violent, cataclysmic vortex that lies outside the narrow corridor of a jump tunnel, or were sent to a place far enough away to make communication or a return trip infeasible. In either case, those missing are presumed dead. Ageira Technologies and Deep Space Engineering urge all citizens to use the prescribed Trade Lanes and Jump Gates and to avoid all contact with jump holes.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Eidolon Star
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>The Eidolon Star, under Captain Daron Kells, was the most lightly armed of the Zoner expedition 13 freighters but carried the largest complement of scientific personnel. Kells was younger than his peers, an academic-turned-explorer whose driving interest was the study of theoretical energy states near black holes. His ship carried custom gravimetric arrays intended to record distortions at unprecedented precision.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>The vessel followed a separate course from the other two, orbiting closer to the singularity’s axis. Logs indicate that the crew detected signals consistent with artificial stabilization fields near the alien structure, suggesting the ruins may have been constructed to interact directly with the black hole. Before Kells could transmit a complete dataset, multiple anomalous entities converged on his trajectory.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>The Eidolon Star’s final maneuver was a desperate descent toward a planet whose orbit was passing in the vicinity of the vessel, engines overdriven past safe limits. The ship was last tracked spiraling into the planet's gravity well, yet fragments of its beacon occasionally resurface - distorted, delayed, and carrying echoes of transmissions never recorded elsewhere explaining a potential new discovery.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Astral Nomad
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>The Astral Nomad was a standard Dromedary-class freighter under the command of Captain Elira Voss, a veteran Zoner navigator known for her meticulous logs and fascination with pre-human stellar ruins. The vessel carried minimal cargo and had been stripped of civilian fittings to accommodate extended-range sensor equipment. Its assignment was reconnaissance: charting the immediate periphery of the Fischer singularity and surveying gravitational anomalies for safe approach vectors.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>According to fragments recovered from her logs, Voss’s crew encountered what appeared to be an alien structure orbiting uncomfortably close to the singularity’s event horizon. The ship’s sensor arrays registered readings inconsistent with known physics-repeating geometric patterns and oscillating energy fields.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>Her last recorded transmission ended abruptly during an evasive maneuver. Automated distress pings later placed the Astral Nomad drifting with catastrophic hull breaches, its engines torn free as though pulled towards a nearby planet where the crew made a desperate last attempt. The transmission also mentioned an unknown artifact located in the vessel's cargo hold...</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Argent Hawk
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>The Argent Hawk was an Eagle very heavy fighter assigned as close escort to the Solstice Runner. Piloted by Commander Ryn Hale, a former House Navy defector turned Zoner mercenary, the ship was outfitted with reinforced reactor shielding and extended fuel cells to sustain long operations at the edge of the singularity. Hale’s role was both reconnaissance and protection, ensuring that the Solstice Runner had cover during its high-risk sensor passes near the alien structure.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>Surviving fragments of encrypted comms suggest Hale was the first to visually acquire the hostile anomalies that later pursued both vessels. He reported “shapes moving without thrust, closing from every vector” moments before weapons systems went live. Hale’s combat log recorded bursts of fire into empty space, sensor returns phasing in and out as though the targets were never fully present.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>The wreck was later found scattered in an elongated field near a gravitational anomaly in the form of a wormhole. The Eagle’s central fuselage was twisted beyond recognition. No ejection signal was detected, and Hale’s remains were never recovered.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Solstice Runner
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>Commanded by Captain Ilar Renn, the Solstice Runner was a heavily modified Dromedary optimized for long-haul endurance, equipped with reinforced shielding and redundant reactor systems. Renn had a reputation among Zoner crews for stubbornness and a habit of ignoring retreat protocols. His ship’s task was to push beyond the sensor perimeter into regions where light itself bent unnaturally, gathering data other crews hesitated to pursue.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>Telemetry fragments suggest Renn’s ship reached the same alien structure minutes after the Astral Nomad, part of the same Zoner expedition 13. His notes, later recovered from databanks, speak of “a brilliance folded into itself” and a surge of coherent signals transmitted in tight-band bursts. The Solstice Runner’s instruments were still processing when unidentified contacts emerged - large, red-tinged anomalies moving with purposeful trajectories.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>The Solstice Runner attempted a high-thrust escape into a denser debris corridor. Wreckage indicates the vessel suffered catastrophic shield collapse before breaching its fuel core. The remains drift in a wide arc around a cracked planet in its vicinity, fragments charred but strangely uniform, as though sectioned deliberately.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Fourchambault Wreck
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>CLASS: La Mole</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>GRAVITY: None</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>DOCKING: No</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>AMENITIES: No</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>CREW: 0</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>Constructed in 663 AGS (747 AS), Fourchambault quickly grew to become a symbol of the Gallic Royal Navy's might in Languedoc. As the launching point for the inevitable invasion of Sirius, the shipyard produced armaments, ship parts, and even warships using Quillan's resources. In 733 AGS (817 AS), Fourchambault briefly fell to The Council, as sympathizers and infiltrated agents among the GRN garrison mutinied. The Council's occupation did not last long however, as their fleet and local supporters were pushed south into the Hebrides by the Crown's counterattack the following year. The GRN quickly boarded the station, and after repairing hasty sabotage efforts, returned the shipyard to service.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>For the rest of the war, the grandiose installation repaired warships and logistics vessels damaged during the Invasion of Sirius. This made the facility a primary target for local Maquis terrorists, who successfully struck the station several times. As a result, the Gallic Monarchy was forced to maintain a significant garrison at all times, drawing troops away from the frontlines. In the chaos of the war's end and the collapse of the GRN, the shipyard was quickly seized by Provence's Minarchy, and used as a bargaining chip to secure their place in the newly created Confederacy.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>When the Kusari Naval Forces invaded the system in 742 AGS (827 AS), the Gallic Confederacy committed significant reserves to holding Fourchambault. After several grinding, attritional battles, Kusari occupied the Ales junction, seizing the station. It was not until The Enclave's counter-attack and the creation of the Gallic Union later that year, that the Kusari presence was dislodged. Fourchambault was scuttled before Kusari withdrew, denying its use to Gallia. Following the war's end, the wreckage was shunted into the nearby Leucate Debris Field, where ALG has since begun salvage operations.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Embrun
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>CLASS: Normandie</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>CREW: N/A</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>ARMAMENT: N/A</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>The Normandie battleship design was first deployed around 656 AGS (740 AS) for offensive assault purposes. These ships were produced in large numbers by royal Gallic shipyards until the early 730s (810s), when the battles of the Second Gallic Civil War revealed several critical flaws in the ships’ construction. Existing vessels were retrofitted to correct various defects, but no new Normandies were built - instead the modernized Richelieu class was developed. Normandie battleships formed the bulk of Gallia’s original Sirius invasion forces.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>The Embrun was deployed in 710 AGS (794 AS) and saw initial service against The Council, before joining the invasion of Bretonia in 735 AGS (819 AS). Using irregular tactics, it struck military and civilian targets across Newcastle and Manchester, quickly accruing a merciless reputation amid accusations of war crimes. It is believed that the Embrun topped the Bretonian Armed Force's most wanted list for several years, gaining an enormous bounty in the process. Commanded by Gallic Royal Intelligence special forces, the Embrun's squadrons were responsible for devious hit and run strategies that pinned Newcastle's fleets, preventing them from supporting the Allied efforts during the devastating Siege of New London.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>Following the war's disastrous end in 742 AGS (826 AS), the Embrun was stranded behind Bretonian lines and unable to retreat to the Gallic Enclave in the Hebrides. Efforts to resupply by extorting Newcastle's Gaians were initially successful, however their compliance was a ruse to buy time for vengeful Gaian reinforcements to converge from across Bretonia. The improvised force struck the Embrun at an agreed supply rendezvous in the Craster Nebula early the next year. Guided by a local freelancer, the damaged battleship fled through a previously uncharted Jump Hole as a desperate means of escape. Little is known about the Embrun's activities until it reappeared later that year to aid Confederal forces during Kusari's Invasion of Gallia.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>The battleship famously turned the tide of the Battle of Agde when it used a cloaking device to ambush the Battleship Yamaguchi, destroying its reactor. The Embrun was subject to withering counter-fire from the surrounding Kusari fleet, and broke in half after its hangar fuel tanks exploded. Regardless, the Yamaguchi's loss threw Kusari's forces into disarray, dooming the Languedoc advance. The Embrun's surviving crew members were hailed as heroes and have since been posted to senior positions throughout the Gallic Union fleet. The battleship's remains are now being salvaged at Briancon Station, under strict GNI supervision.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: La Fierte
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>CLASS: Charlamagne (Redemption)</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>CREW: N/A</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>ARMAMENT: N/A</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>The Charlemagne battleships were designed around 676 AGS (760 AS), specifically for defensive and support purposes. Battleships of this class were configured to hold and maintain large numbers of fighters and cover them with powerful point defense turrets. The La Fierte was deployed from Rambouillet Shipyard in 697 AGS (781 AS), serving unremarkably until it was assigned to the Marne Pacification Fleet in 712 AGS (796 AS). One of several Council infiltrated warships, the La Fierte defected upon entering Marne orbit, initiating the Battle of Champagne and contributing to the Council's liberation of the system. Due to their dramatic sorties against royal assaults, the Le Fierte's strike wings quickly became the pride of Marne.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>The Invasion of Sirius lessened the GRN's focus on Champagne, allowing the La Fierte to strike into Picardy in the hope of inciting unrest on Planet Amiens. When news of war crimes and military collapse trickled back to the core systems in 742 AGS (826 AS), the Le Fierte launched an attack on Amiens. The Battleship Samur immediately surrendered, while Le Fierte's fighters supported revolts across the planet in toppling the leaderless Royal Army regiments. Having secured Picardy for the Gallic Republic, the battleship pushed into to Ile-de-France to support the planned Council assault on New Paris. In the uncomfortable peace following the emergence of the Gallic Confederacy, the La Fierte returned to Picardy to suppress Enclave holdouts.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>Following much needed repairs and maintenance, the battleship was assigned to Zurich to oversee the completion of the trade corridor connecting to Rheinland. Within days of the Alsace Passage's opening in 743 AGS (827 AS), Rheinland devolved into civil war. The Confederacy reeled with shock as the Red Hessians conquered Cologne and the Federalist battleship Karlsruhe fled into Gallic territory. Fearing an incident that would drag them into the conflict, the La Fierte was ordered to intern the battleship. While negotiating the Karlsruhe's surrender, Captain Michaud instead agreed to provide supplies for an assault on Cologne, intending to dislodge the Red Hessians and re-open trade.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>When the Karlsruhe eventually departed, it slipped through Cologne and instead invaded Stuttgart. Outraged, the Confederal Navy would have court martialled Captain Michaud for insubordination, were it not for the Kusari Invasion of Gallia. The La Fierte was rushed to Languedoc to support the collapsing Minarchy positions, arriving to reinforce the Confederal lines during the Battle of Agde. The La Fierte's strike wings performed according to the mythos they had developed during the Second Gallic Civil War, punching the holes in the Battleship Yamaguchi's escorts that the Embrun later exploited. The La Fierte's valiant but fatal last stand brought time for the joint Confederal-Enclave counter assault that ended Kusari's advance towards Ile-de-France.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

The La Fierte was rushed to Languedoc to support the collapsing Minarchy positions, arriving to reinforce the Confederal lines during the Battle of Agde. The La Fierte's strike wings performed according to the mythos they had developed during the Second Gallic Civil War, punching the holes in the Battleship Yamaguchi's escorts that the Embrun later exploited. The La Fierte's valiant but fatal last stand brought time for the joint Confederal-Enclave counter assault that ended Kusari's advance towards Ile-de-France.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Yamaguchi
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>CLASS: Bakumatsu</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>CREW: N/A</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>ARMAMENT: N/A</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>The Battleship Yamaguchi was among the first generation of the Bakumatsu class, deployed in 813 AS to bolster Kusari's ambitions in the Taus. The Yamaguchi -- as all Bakumatsu battleships -- was criticized for the lack of innovation in its design, which Samura had produced as a minor modernization on the much older Meiji class. The Battleships Yamaguchi and Nagasaki were the speartip of the KNF's expeditionary force during the 813 AS Tau War with Bretonia. This culminated with the Invasion of Leeds in 816 AS, and the capture of Stokes Mining Station the following year. During a tour of the front lines by Emperor Jien Kogen in 818 AS, disaster struck when Gallia launched the Invasion of Sirius.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>The Gallic Royal Navy poured into the Taus, slamming into the flanks of Kusari's supply lines. Caught between the Gallic fleet and Bretonian defenses, the 8 Day War saw much of Kusari's Tau fleet destroyed, and the expeditionary force stranded abroad. When a coup toppled the government in the Emperor's absence, the Yamaguchi and Nagasaki refused to recognize the new Republic's legitimacy. The so-called Exiles pledged their service to the Emperor, and swore to retake their home. The Yamaguchi was then contacted by Council Gallic dissidents, who provided a route to their new refuge in Roussillon. They hoped the Exiles would restore a Kusari that was hostile to the Gallic crown, opening another front in the war.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>For several years, the Yamaguchi resupplied from Council bases, while striking Gallic and Kusari collaborator targets across the Taus. In 824 AS, both Exile battleships reunited to initiate the Kusari Civil War with the Kyushu Uprising. Following reunification and restoration of the Imperial line the following year, the Yamaguchi received extensive repairs and modernization. This delayed its deployment to the Saigon War against Rheinland, which saw Kusari repulsed from Sigma-21. The Yamaguchi instead reinforced the Hyono in Honshu, cutting Rheinland supply lines and helping to force the eventual peace. She then patrolled the Sigma border, before being recalled to Kyushu in 827 AS, amid disputes with the Crayter Republic.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>The KNF expelled the Republic from Tau-31, however this was a pretext to maneuver their fleets closer to the Gallic border for a surprise invasion. Gallic Confederal forces were shocked when the Hyono, Nagasaki, and Yamaguchi fleets swung north into Tau-23, rapidly breaching Languedoc. The Yamaguchi then led a flanking assault, decisively defeating Confederal forces at the Battle of Sete. The Battle of Agde marked the turning point of Kusari's campaign -- after dispatching the Le Fierte and pressing towards the Ile-de-France Jump Gate, the Yamaguchi was crippled by the Battleship Embrun. Decloaking and launching salvos of torpedoes and trebuchets at short range, the Yamaguchi's reactor detonated before the crew could react.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Hyono
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>CLASS: Toitsu</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>CREW: N/A</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>ARMAMENT: N/A</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>One of the frontrunners of the Toitsu class, the Hyono deployed from Kure Shipyard in 825 AS, shortly before the Saigon War with Rheinland. Following the destruction of Ibusuki Survey Platform in Sigma-21, the Hyono fleet was dispatched to aid the Gas Miners Guild against the Rheinland Military. While her expanded hangar bays initially allowed generous strike wings to contest Planet Saigon, the tide dramatically turned with the arrival of Rheinland reinforcements. By exploiting Sigma-21's open space, the Bayern and Westfalen fleets forced their enemies to fight on unfavorable terms, inflicting heavy casualties. The Hyono was damaged during the 826 AS rout back to Honshu, where it regrouped to rally a defense.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>Using the cover of Honshu's Hiryo Cloud, the Hyono and other KNF elements succeeded in holding the Rheinland fleets at bay, while severing their Sigma-21 supply lines. Following the war's end, the battleship was sent for extensive repairs and refits at Kure Shipyard. Its next assignment in 827 AS shocked Sirius, when a significant Kusari military buildup along the Tau borders was justified as a dispute with the Crayter Republic. While the KNF did then expel the Republic from Tau-31, this was a pretext for maneuvering their fleets closer to the Gallic border to launch a surprise invasion. As a result, Gallic Confederal forces were taken by surprise when the Hyono, Nagasaki, and Yamaguchi fleets swung north into Tau-23. </TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>The Kusari fleet rapidly scattered the local Tau garrison and destroyed Cheronsee Outpost, to avoid a time-consuming boarding attempt. Breaching the Languedoc Jump Gate, the Hyono was met by the Battleship Cassard, which was heavily damaged and driven off. The Hyono then advanced with the Nagasaki alongside the Trade Lanes, and was responsible for disabling Nimes Station while the Nagasaki destroyed Quillan's spaceports. It later participated in the Battles of Ales, scuttling Fourchambalt Shipyard late in the year when the joint Confederal-Enclave counter-offensive was launched. The Hyono was eventually lost while retreating back towards the Taus, falling to the Warwolf cannon of the Enclave's Battleship Rocroi.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Rocroi
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>CLASS: Richelieu</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>CREW: N/A</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>ARMAMENT: N/A</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>The Richelieu battleships were designed around 731 AGS (815 AS) to correct design flaws identified in the Normandie class during the Second Gallic Civil War. Richelieu battleships provided a blend of withering firepower and heavy armor, built around the fearsome Warwolf spinal cannons. By the time of the Gallic invasion of Sirius, the modernized Richelieus were used as the armored fist of the Gallic Royal Navy, inflicting a deadly toll during their engagements with Bretonia, Kusari and Liberty. As one of the first Richelieus, the Rocroi saw extensive service during the Second Gallic Civil War. Led by Rear Admiral Bastien de Fontenoy, the unwaveringly loyal fleet was charged with the defense of the King and Planet New Paris.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>When the GRN collapsed in 742 AGS (826 AS), the Rocroi executed plans to evacuate the King. To their shock, the King had already vanished, consumed by paranoia that the Navy was planning to betray him. Instead, the Rocroi prepared Ile-de-France's garrison for a forlorn and bloody resistance against The Council's looming assault. When de Fontenoy and his crew received a ceasefire order from the Grand Duchy of Burgundy, it was seen as a gross betrayal of their oath. In the chaos of the Gallic Confederacy's formation, the Rocroi and its fleet slipped away to Burgundy, hoping to find noble supporters to aid in toppling Grand Duke Valentin Trintignant, and restore the absent King Charles at the head of the Gallic Enclave.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>Her campaign against Confederal and Maquis forces in Burgundy was cut short by the Kusari Invasion the following year. As the situation became increasingly dire for Gallia, the Confederation was forced into negotiations with the Enclave on reintegration. As a result, the Enclave ordered the Rocroi south, to support a renewed counteroffensive in Languedoc. Significanty, the Rocroi succeeded in destroying the retreating Battleship Hyono with its Warwolf cannon, before being dispatched in turn by the Nagasaki's fleet. The battleship's survivors have since been awarded prestigious postings throughout the Gallic Union fleet, with now-Admiral de Fontenoy appointed to lead Compiegne Naval Academy.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Ile-de-France Jump Hole
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TRA data="65281" mask="-31" def="30"/><TEXT>***GRAVITATIONAL ANOMALY DETECTED***</TEXT><PARA/><TRA data="96" mask="-31" def="-1"/><TEXT> </TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>Magnetic and gravimetric readings are consistent with a Jump Hole -- a natural phenomenon that functions similar to a Jump Gate, though the hazards associated with traveling through a Jump Hole remain largely unknown. Like Jump Gates, jump holes are semi-permeable areas in real-space that have a tendency to breach the natural boundaries of linear time and space. Unlike Jump Gates, though, these anomalies occur naturally and so are both unpredictable and unstable. Traveling through jump holes is a risky proposition at best. Though some have been charted and, based on accounts from ships that have accidentally encountered them, have had their exit points logged, just as many ships have never been heard from again. It is believed that these ships were either crushed in the violent, cataclysmic vortex that lies outside the narrow corridor of a jump tunnel, or were sent to a place far enough away to make communication or a return trip infeasible. In either case, those missing are presumed dead. Ageira Technologies and Deep Space Engineering urge all citizens to use the prescribed Trade Lanes and Jump Gates and to avoid all contact with jump holes.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Epinal
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>The Epinal was an aging Richelieu-class Battleship that saw much of its service being deployed in the Champagne and Lorraine systems to counter Council activity. In the late stages of the Second Gallic Civil War, it was the first ship to stand down after receiving permission from the newly-proclaimed Grand Duchy of Burgundy. Subsequently, it remained a vanguard of the new Gallic Confederacy in Lorraine, whilst also guarding the important border fortress that overlooked the boundary with the Taus.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>When Kusari launched their invasion of Gallia, the Epinal was the first line of defence against the advancing Kusari forces. Forced to cede more and more territory to the invaders, the Epinal was withdrawn to Burgundy, having bought enough time for the Confederacy to move ships to reinforce her once she arrived.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>Slowly withdrawing towards the Picardy Jump Gate, the Epinal was the core of the fleet that stood between the Naval Forces and the Gallic Core Worlds. Shortly before reinforcements were due to arrive from deeper in Gallia, the KNF launched a desperate attack to take the Jump Gate, which would have allowed them to hold there and consolidate their position. Determined to hold out, the Epinal led her fleet in a brilliant defense, managing to force the KNF forces to withdraw in the face of their unrelenting firepower.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>This would also lead to her undoing. One of the attacking KNF ships, the Ueda, had been disabled partway through the battle. Managing to restore power to their ship, the Ueda’s crew launched into a headlong attack directly into the teeth of the Epinal, knowing that any attempt to retreat would simply lead to their own demise. Seeing this attack coming but with little time for her more conventional weapons to be brought to bear, the Epinal began charging her massive Warwolf cannon, hoping to destroy the charging Ueda in a single well placed shot.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>The Ueda struck the Epinal just as the massive cannon finished charging, but before it could fire its devastating payload, feeding back into the main reactor and causing a critical failure. The resulting explosion, believed to be the largest man-made explosion in recorded history, consumed both ships, as well as many smaller ships in the immediate vicinity. The explosion - visible as far away as Nevers - caused the entire battle to come to a stand still for a brief moment, which was only broken when the nearby gate activated and the Gallic reinforcements started to pour through.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>The Epinal was an aging Richelieu-class Battleship that saw much of its service being deployed in the Champagne and Lorraine systems to counter Council activity. In the late stages of the Second Gallic Civil War, it was the first ship to stand down after receiving permission from the newly-proclaimed Grand Duchy of Burgundy. Subsequently, it remained a vanguard of the new Gallic Confederacy in Lorraine, whilst also guarding the important border fortress that overlooked the boundary with the Taus.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>When Kusari launched their invasion of Gallia, the Epinal was the first line of defence against the advancing Kusari forces. Forced to cede more and more territory to the invaders, the Epinal was withdrawn to Burgundy, having bought enough time for the Confederacy to move ships to reinforce her once she arrived.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>Slowly withdrawing towards the Picardy Jump Gate, the Epinal was the core of the fleet that stood between the Naval Forces and the Gallic Core Worlds. Shortly before reinforcements were due to arrive from deeper in Gallia, the KNF launched a desperate attack to take the Jump Gate, which would have allowed them to hold there and consolidate their position. Determined to hold out, the Epinal led her fleet in a brilliant defense, managing to force the KNF forces to withdraw in the face of their unrelenting firepower.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>This would also lead to her undoing. One of the attacking KNF ships, the Ueda, had been disabled partway through the battle. Managing to restore power to their ship, the Ueda’s crew launched into a headlong attack directly into the teeth of the Epinal, knowing that any attempt to retreat would simply lead to their own demise. Seeing this attack coming but with little time for her more conventional weapons to be brought to bear, the Epinal began charging her massive Warwolf cannon, hoping to destroy the charging Ueda in a single well placed shot.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>The Ueda struck the Epinal just as the massive cannon finished charging, but before it could fire its devastating payload, feeding back into the main reactor and causing a critical failure. The resulting explosion, believed to be the largest man-made explosion in recorded history, consumed both ships, as well as many smaller ships in the immediate vicinity. The explosion - visible as far away as Nevers - caused the entire battle to come to a stand still for a brief moment, which was only broken when the nearby gate activated and the Gallic reinforcements started to pour through.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Ueda
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>The Ueda was a Toitsu-class Battleship launched shortly before the onset of the invasion of Gallia. With her construction having been held up by the outbreak of the Civil War, she actually launched after the first of the new Showa-class Battleships, and as such crew priorities were given to the more advanced ships. This meant that the crew of the Ueda was assembled at the last minute, and the hope was that any necessary training could happen during deployment.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>This strategy failed however, as the rapid advance of the Hamamatsu and her fleet into Gallia stretched Kusari’s limited manpower reserves to their limit. Being forced to deploy the Ueda regardless of the inexperience of her crew, she arrived to reinforce the fleet just in time to join the initial push into Burgundy. During this initial engagement, the Ueda was targeted by a flotilla of Gallant-class Cruisers, suffering heavy damage to her engines in the fighting. Without the ability to withdraw the ship for repairs, it was decided that the Ueda would instead assume a position at the very front of the fleet, helping to reduce the need for the ship to maneuver.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>This led to the ship also taking increased fire, and a well-timed shot from the Hossegor knocked out all power to the ship, leaving her completely defenseless. Managing to weather the fire directed at her until the crew managed to restore power, the inexperienced officers of the Ueda thought that she would be able to engage the Epinal as it advanced towards the fleet. Shortly after they began their assault, another blow disabled all weapons aboard, and with no other option the Ueda rammed the Epinal at full speed.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>The resulting explosion caused a shockwave that killed all hands aboard both ships, and the Ueda now lies in space next to her nemesis, the Epinal.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Saulx
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>Much like its fleet’s flagship - the Epinal - the Sault spent a large portion of its service in regions held by the Gallic Royal Navy that were contested by the Council. During the closing days of the Second Gallic Civil War, the crew of the Saulx was unlike any other in her fleet -- a mixture of loyalists to the King, sympathizers of the Council, and a small number of personnel forcibly drafted into the Navy. The result was an incident that almost resulted in the ship being fired upon by its counterparts, largely due to an initial refusal to stand down upon receiving the order from Nevers.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>The Confederacy did not overlook the incident, deciding that the best course of action would be to continue deploying the Saulx in the fringe regions of the state, ensuring that the crew was kept busy by the many enemies Gallia still had. In the initial days of the invasion by Kusari, the Saulx was the first to receive the baptism of fire from the Hamamatsu, resulting in a large portion of the hull being blown off and having to be sent to Avallon Fortress for emergency repairs.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>Despite their differences the crew stood united in their fight against the Kusari Naval Forces, making their final stand in the northern regions of Burgundy and becoming one of the very last casualties of the war.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Les Vosges
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>Once representative of the new Charlemagne-class Battleships built by the Confederacy, the Les Voges and its sister ship, the Hossegor, saw little action before the outbreak of war with Kusari. Having spent such little time training, the obvious result was a lack of experience both for the crew and officers. In spite of substantial efforts to adapt to the changing situation on the battlefield, the Les Voges posed no challenge to the Matsumoto and Hamamatsu battlegroups.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>Its wreck is in a highly radioactive state that prevents relocation, and the local Junkers have begun preying upon its components, drawing the ire of the Gallic Union's forces.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Tawara
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>Like her sister ship the Shimada, the Tawara was a state of the art Showa-class Battleship, expanding on the capabilities of the older Tokugawa-class. Designed by the Kusari Naval Forces to face off against the Valor-class, which had torn its way through their fleet in the Taus at the start of the Gallic Invasion, the Showa-class were heavily armed and armored in an attempt to match the Gallic Royal Navy ship for ship. The Tawara took this theory to the next level, with several additional mounting points being added for heavy weaponry, sacrificing defensive capability, but allowing the ship to act as a mobile artillery platform for the fleet.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>During the invasion of Burgundy, it played one such crucial role when it was ordered to launch a devastating barrage upon Avallon Fortress, and later Nevers itself, footage of which was broadcast across Sirius. As the KNF was driven ever-closer to defeat, the Tawara continued to act in a support role until the onset of the retreat from Gallia, quickly becoming the center of the force which the rest of the fleet was arrayed around.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>Led by a mishmash crew of Civil War and Tau War veterans, the Tawara refused to retreat with the rest of the fleet, knowing that if a delaying action was not fought, then the entire fleet would likely be picked apart piece by piece. Though successful in their chosen mission, the Tawara was always doomed to fall, with most of the crew dying at their stations as the ship’s systems failed one by one. It was the last Kusari warship disabled by the Confederacy, the smoldering wreck a valuable prize for hardliners in the soon to form Gallic Union, glad of the retribution carried out against the ship that had so publicly attacked them.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Shimada
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>The Shimada - a state of the art Showa-class Battleship - was designed with the ability to go toe-to-toe with any Valor-class and prevail with ease. The crew was drilled to the highest of the Kusari Naval Forces standards, with frequent exercises taking place to simulate any possible scenario that the ship’s command crew could think of. This rigorous training proved extremely valuable when Kusari declared war on Gallia, as the invasion gave free reign to the veteran Kusari forces to devastate both the military and populace of the Confederacy.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>With a swift move, the Shimada, alongside the rest of the forces gathered, crippled the Gallic defenses in Lorraine, then proceeded to advance into Burgundy, putting even New Paris at risk of capture. However, the sacrifice of the Epinal and the arrival of fresh ships to the battle forced the Kusari Naval Forces to retreat to a more favorable position in the northern reaches of the system.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>The ship met its demise when the Gallic Navy launched an offensive to pin down the remainder of the Hamamatsu fleet, being the first of several losses that the KNF would suffer at the hands of the vengeful Gallic Navy, suffering heavily under the long range firepower that Gallic Battleships are so well known for.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TRA data="65281" mask="-31" def="30"/><TEXT>***GRAVITATIONAL ANOMALY DETECTED***</TEXT><PARA/><TRA data="96" mask="-31" def="-1"/><TEXT> </TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>Magnetic and gravimetric readings are consistent with a Jump Hole -- a natural phenomenon that functions similar to a Jump Gate, though the hazards associated with traveling through a Jump Hole remain largely unknown. Like Jump Gates, jump holes are semi-permeable areas in real-space that have a tendency to breach the natural boundaries of linear time and space. Unlike Jump Gates, though, these anomalies occur naturally and so are both unpredictable and unstable. Traveling through jump holes is a risky proposition at best. Though some have been charted and, based on accounts from ships that have accidentally encountered them, have had their exit points logged, just as many ships have never been heard from again. It is believed that these ships were either crushed in the violent, cataclysmic vortex that lies outside the narrow corridor of a jump tunnel, or were sent to a place far enough away to make communication or a return trip infeasible. In either case, those missing are presumed dead. Ageira Technologies and Deep Space Engineering urge all citizens to use the prescribed Trade Lanes and Jump Gates and to avoid all contact with jump holes.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>Rheinland's history in this system is... clouded. There was a great deal of activity here in the years leading up to the Colony Wars, although none alive can say how that came to be. Most of this we know of only indirectly, as records were thoroughly destroyed as the Niemann regime collapsed. The scale of funds embezzled into this system was immense.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>I am based on Dagger Outpost as a liaison for the MND. Rheinland has an intense interest in The Core's work here, and partially funds their operations in exchange for preferential access. We were forced to end direct deployments into Omega-55 with the collapse of the Omega-11 Jump Hole in 822 AS. The Core has effectively acted as our proxy since then.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>Kusari has a vested interest in monitoring the Bretonian campaign. It was enabled by our technology after all. The theory underpinning it is sound of course, however the operation of paired Jump Drives to sustain a logistics bridge is a high intensity use case that will provide excellent field data.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TRA data="65281" mask="-31" def="30"/><TEXT>***GRAVITATIONAL ANOMALY DETECTED***</TEXT><PARA/><TRA data="96" mask="-31" def="-1"/><TEXT> </TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>Magnetic and gravimetric readings are consistent with a Jump Hole -- a natural phenomenon that functions similar to a Jump Gate, though the hazards associated with traveling through a Jump Hole remain largely unknown. Like Jump Gates, jump holes are semi-permeable areas in real-space that have a tendency to breach the natural boundaries of linear time and space. Unlike Jump Gates, though, these anomalies occur naturally and so are both unpredictable and unstable. Traveling through jump holes is a risky proposition at best. Though some have been charted and, based on accounts from ships that have accidentally encountered them, have had their exit points logged, just as many ships have never been heard from again. It is believed that these ships were either crushed in the violent, cataclysmic vortex that lies outside the narrow corridor of a jump tunnel, or were sent to a place far enough away to make communication or a return trip infeasible. In either case, those missing are presumed dead. Ageira Technologies and Deep Space Engineering urge all citizens to use the prescribed Trade Lanes and Jump Gates and to avoid all contact with jump holes.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: The Novembrist
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>The Novembrist was the callsign of a lone bounty hunter operating in the deep southern sectors, known for pursuing contracts far beyond conventional patrol routes. Records link the pilot to multiple high-value captures across Bretonian and Border World space, though no confirmed identity was ever established. His vessel, a heavily customized Crusader, bore no insignia other than its codename painted in faded white along the hull. The ship’s last registered pursuit took him into the Cayman system, trailing a Red Hessian fugitive rumored to have sought passage deeper into the Omegas.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>Navigation logs retrieved from the derelict indicate that The Novembrist maintained pursuit through the Red Western Nebula, where ion storms disrupt long-range sensors. The pilot’s commentary, stored in bursts of encrypted voice data, notes erratic gravitic fluctuations and a sudden signal spike ahead of the Hessian’s last known vector. Moments later, the fighter encountered an anomaly: a shifting, crimson distortion described by the hunter as “a hollow sun, beating in silence.” The Hessian’s trail vanished in that instant, leaving The Novembrist without bearings.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>The wreck was later discovered adrift at low power near the nebula’s fringe. The hull showed no signs of combat, yet all systems had failed sequentially as if power had been siphoned away. The cockpit canopy was sealed, but no pilot was present inside. To this day, the Novembrist’s ship remains anchored in the nebula by weak gravitational pull, its beacon still faintly transmitting the last line of encrypted voice data; words fragmented beyond recognition, repeating in uneven intervals as if echoing from the anomaly itself.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Lapin
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>The wreckage of the Lapin, flown by Remi Corriveau. A renowned ace in the Council Navy, Corriveau served as an officer of the OCI during the Confederacy and the subsequent invasion by Kusari. He would flee Gallia after the royalist takeover of the Office in the wake of the conflict, his skill as a pilot landing him a lucrative post with the Core’s paramilitary.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>His proficiency and adaptability would quickly earn him the position of a squadron leader. It was shortly after this promotion that Corriveau and his squadron were assigned to the Edenvale as escorts for its upcoming mission. Further reinforced by the WV Ensis, the squadron and its charge departed for the deep Omegas, never to be seen again.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>The ship’s hull is riddled with damage typically inflicted by neutron weaponry, the killing shot having struck the main powerplant. The ship's blackbox is severely damaged. The remaining snippets of data indicate the expedition went through multiple engagements against unspecified attackers. The final entry suggests Corriveau was ambushed by an unidentified freighter.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Pejesapo
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>The wreckage of Pejesapo, a Centurion-class fighter flown by Diego Moliner. Unlike his wingmen, Moliner was a largely unremarkable irregular, working perimeter security for Leon Base for most of his career. He was, however, a close friend of Cleonic Cavaleri, the founder of the infamous Cerbero squadron. It was through this connection that he found himself recruited for the team, proving himself as a reliable fighter who prioritized the safety of his fellow pilots.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>Like the rest of the Cerbero squadron, Moliner was last seen trailing a Core convoy through the southern Omega systems.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>Analysis of the wreckage indicates the ship was crippled by a salvo of particle blasts, then finished off in the ensuing battle. The onboard logs are damaged, the remaining data indicating the Pejesapo used its armor to absorb the opening volley of an ambush, though the resulting damage proved too much for the ship to handle.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Bahir Dar
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>DIAMETER: 2,890 km</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>MASS: 1.72 x 10e22 kg kg</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>TERRAIN: Barren</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>TEMPERATURE: 700°C to 1,400°C</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>ESCAPE VELOCITY: 3.4 km/sec</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT> </TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>A small but violent moon, constantly reshaped by volcanic activity. Its orbit around the frozen world of Tija generates intense tidal forces, keeping its interior molten and its surface unstable. Lava flows stretch for kilometers, and eruptions are frequent enough to make landings a high-risk operation. Anything left on the surface for too long will either melt or be buried under fresh layers of rock.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Planet Tija
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>DIAMETER: 6,471 km</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>MASS: 3.12 x 10e24 kg</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>TERRAIN: Arctic</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>TEMPERATURE: -220°C to -180°C</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>ESCAPE VELOCITY: 8.4 km/sec</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT> </TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>An inhospitable, frozen world with a thin atmosphere orbiting Omega-2's central star. The surface is mostly solid ice, broken up by jagged ridges and deep crevasses. There are traces of past geological activity, but these days, it’s little more than a lifeless, frozen desert. The temperature is low enough to make most materials brittle. No native life, no real atmosphere, just an endless stretch of ice under an empty sky.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Planet Aksum
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>DIAMETER: 27,551 km</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>MASS: 1.55 x 10e26 kg</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>TERRAIN: N/A</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>TEMPERATURE: N/A</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>ESCAPE VELOCITY: 60.2 km/sec</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT> </TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>A yellow gas giant with an unpredictable atmosphere, orbiting Omega-2's central star. Its upper layers are in constant motion, with storms that stretch for thousands of kilometers and winds that can easily rip apart unshielded ships. The deeper one goes, the pressure and heat skyrocket, making it impossible to explore beyond a certain depth. Strong electromagnetic fields interfere with most standard sensors, and its gravity well can easily claim careless pilots underestimating the planet's dangers.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Mekele
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>DIAMETER: 3,924 km</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>MASS: 2.19 x 10e23 kg</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>TERRAIN: Barren</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>TEMPERATURE: -80°C to 15°C</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>ESCAPE VELOCITY: 2.3 km/sec</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT> </TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>A barren, reddish moon orbiting Omega-2's distant blue star. Its thin atmosphere doesn’t provide much protection from radiation, and its surface is covered in craters and wind-carved rock formations. Occasional dust storms sweep across the landscape, making navigation difficult. While there are no signs of life, traces of ice have been found beneath the surface, making it a potential stop for deep-space operations.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>I have been posted to the Essex as a technical attache and analyst. There is an Office of Intelligence agent who serves as my attendant and bodyguard. This seems unnecessary while I remain aboard a Bretonian battleship, however he insists the Mollys will murder me without hesitation if given the chance.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>Bowex is the primary supplier of the Bretonia Armed Forces, and unfortunately that means in times of war, we get sent to the front. It was true during the Gallic Invasion, and it's true now too. Today I was shipping H-Fuel to the Essex, which meant I didn't need to go through that horrendous Jump Hole into Dublin.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>The Bretonians are deploying a minefield in Dublin to protect the jump bridge. This is prudent, of course. There are many examples of Jump Gates being safely ensconced in a protective minefield. A Jump Drive should react no differently... in theory. We await the minefield's completion with great anticipation.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>
