objects.name: New Tokyo Jump Hole
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TRA data="65281" mask="-31" def="30"/><TEXT>***GRAVITATIONAL ANOMALY DETECTED***</TEXT><PARA/><TRA data="96" mask="-31" def="-1"/><TEXT> </TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>Magnetic and gravimetric readings are consistent with a Jump Hole -- a natural phenomenon that functions similar to a Jump Gate, though the hazards associated with traveling through a Jump Hole remain largely unknown. Like Jump Gates, jump holes are semi-permeable areas in real-space that have a tendency to breach the natural boundaries of linear time and space. Unlike Jump Gates, though, these anomalies occur naturally and so are both unpredictable and unstable. Traveling through jump holes is a risky proposition at best. Though some have been charted and, based on accounts from ships that have accidentally encountered them, have had their exit points logged, just as many ships have never been heard from again. It is believed that these ships were either crushed in the violent, cataclysmic vortex that lies outside the narrow corridor of a jump tunnel, or were sent to a place far enough away to make communication or a return trip infeasible. In either case, those missing are presumed dead. Ageira Technologies and Deep Space Engineering urge all citizens to use the prescribed Trade Lanes and Jump Gates and to avoid all contact with jump holes.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Fort Wakkanai Wreck
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>Constructed in 825 AS, Fort Wakkanai was a large Naval facility situated strategically at the edge of the Unyo cloud to serve multiple roles, most importantly as a training facility for new pilots. Trainees based out of Wakkanai fly CAP and drill for advanced maneuvers in Unyo for a minimum of 200 hours before being transferred to postings around Kusari. Naval Statistics showed that trainees from Wakkanai have a 40% lower mortality rate, a rate expected to drop even further in the future.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>For pilots permanently posted at Wakkanai, the base serves as a beachhead for operations in northern Kusari. Fighter wings spearheaded by gunships bound for the Chugoku and Tohoku systems were not uncommon.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>Fort Wakkanai following the closure of the Tau-53 gate and that proceeded freezing of trade with Gallia in 828 AS, steadily became a needless facility in an inhospitable system. Matters would come to a head following the mothballing of Battleship Sado in 831 AS as the burden of Tohoku patrols fell on Wakkanai. The demise of the station would come as increasingly aggressive Kusari criminals attacked KNF facilities in response to the encroachment on their revenue sources originating from Tau.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Dragonfyre
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TRA data="1" mask="1" def="-2"/><JUST loc="center"/><TEXT>Samura Train "Dragonfyre"</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TRA data="0" mask="1" def="-1"/><JUST loc="left"/><TEXT>A wrecked Ryuujin-class train. Scans are unable to locate traces of life signs.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>Despite the heavily damaged condition of this vessel, some compartments seem to still be pressurized. The black box was accessed recently and is still emitting a low-frequency data signal.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>SUIT-ID: Kaworu - [Heavy breathing can be heard.] Tried my best, but the engine exploded last second. Life support is offline, the oxygen is now part of the Crow. Pretty sure I lost them but me crashing into the rock probably drew attention. Stuff's just not working out for me today. At least I'm still breathing. For now. Gonna be a long suit jump. I'm not going to give up just yet, though. Pilfered all remaining supplies, maybe I can get some makeshift repairs for the escape pod going. Need to find the way back to the Hokkaido jump hole, then all the way to... whatever is out there.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>[PROXIMITY ALERT]</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>SUIT-ID: Kaworu - [A chuckle can be heard.] ... Yeah, they got me. But not the cache. They'll need to fly up the serpentine trail to find it. All the way up to the shattered egg. Hidden in plain sight, really. Who knows. Maybe I can come back and get it. Or I should just cut my losses here.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>Ammo and equipment isn't so much of a problem on an industrial planet. objects.name: Manhattan Docking Ring
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TRA data="65281" mask="-31" def="30"/><TEXT>>>>WARNING: Do not attempt planetary landing without using a Docking Ring.<<<</TEXT><PARA/><TRA data="96" mask="-31" def="-1"/><TEXT> </TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>A docking ring is a piece of orbiting technology that, through the use of super strong crystalline polymers and frictionless bearings, assists the smooth atmospheric entry of any interstellar vessel that has the ability to land. Invented in 130 AS by Ageira Technologies, these 'orbital elevators' almost completely negate the cost of boosting people or materials out of a planetary gravity well. Docking rings revolutionized exploration and industry almost overnight, opening up entire systems for commercial exploration and exploitation.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>Ageira Technologies licenses this technology to the other houses, who in turn agree to design all ships (except for special exploratory and survey vessels), to work with the docking ring system.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Liberty Battlecruiser
objects.infocard:
AUGUSTA -- 832 AS -- The fires of revolt still smolder on Malta, but we have no time to count our losses and mourn our dead. We are forced to steel our hearts and once more rise to defend ourselves from outsiders who would see the Outcasts destroyed.

We of course speak of the Corsairs, who exploited our people's moment of tragedy to seize Freeport 9 as a forward base. The Corsair occupation of the Freeport represents an existential threat to the Maltese people, and their raids upon our very home cannot and will not be tolerated. The Battlecruiser Augusta has led a force into Omicron Theta with orders to destroy the station and its biodomes, disrupt the Corsairs, and annihilate the Artifact trade that funds them.

Already we have won a great victory by striking down the Battleship Fes, with the Battleship Delos surely soon to join it in the grave. The Dons have promised a handsome payment to the cartel of each pilot that kills a Corsair in Omicron Theta.

objects.name: Cortez Jump Hole
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TRA data="65281" mask="-31" def="30"/><TEXT>***GRAVITATIONAL ANOMALY DETECTED***</TEXT><PARA/><TRA data="96" mask="-31" def="-1"/><TEXT> </TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>Magnetic and gravimetric readings are consistent with a Jump Hole -- a natural phenomenon that functions similar to a Jump Gate, though the hazards associated with traveling through a Jump Hole remain largely unknown. Like Jump Gates, jump holes are semi-permeable areas in real-space that have a tendency to breach the natural boundaries of linear time and space. Unlike Jump Gates, though, these anomalies occur naturally and so are both unpredictable and unstable. Traveling through jump holes is a risky proposition at best. Though some have been charted and, based on accounts from ships that have accidentally encountered them, have had their exit points logged, just as many ships have never been heard from again. It is believed that these ships were either crushed in the violent, cataclysmic vortex that lies outside the narrow corridor of a jump tunnel, or were sent to a place far enough away to make communication or a return trip infeasible. In either case, those missing are presumed dead. Ageira Technologies and Deep Space Engineering urge all citizens to use the prescribed Trade Lanes and Jump Gates and to avoid all contact with jump holes.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>A jump gate is a conveyance technology that allows instantaneous travel between two distinct points in space using technology pioneered by Ageira Technologies and built by Deep Space Engineering in 130 AS. According to the annual Ageira Technologies Shareholder Report, 'jump gate technology is designed to gather and amplify certain permeable tendencies in real-space and connect them to other congruent points elsewhere in the sector, while still maintaining the structural integrity and stability of the channel created by this process and of the object passing through it.'</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>Ageira Technologies and Deep Space Engineering continue to survey other potential jump point candidates and expect to provide connections with other areas further and further away as their research continues.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Kepler Jump Hole
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TRA data="65281" mask="-31" def="30"/><TEXT>***GRAVITATIONAL ANOMALY DETECTED***</TEXT><PARA/><TRA data="96" mask="-31" def="-1"/><TEXT> </TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>Magnetic and gravimetric readings are consistent with a Jump Hole -- a natural phenomenon that functions similar to a Jump Gate, though the hazards associated with traveling through a Jump Hole remain largely unknown. Like Jump Gates, jump holes are semi-permeable areas in real-space that have a tendency to breach the natural boundaries of linear time and space. Unlike Jump Gates, though, these anomalies occur naturally and so are both unpredictable and unstable. Traveling through jump holes is a risky proposition at best. Though some have been charted and, based on accounts from ships that have accidentally encountered them, have had their exit points logged, just as many ships have never been heard from again. It is believed that these ships were either crushed in the violent, cataclysmic vortex that lies outside the narrow corridor of a jump tunnel, or were sent to a place far enough away to make communication or a return trip infeasible. In either case, those missing are presumed dead. Ageira Technologies and Deep Space Engineering urge all citizens to use the prescribed Trade Lanes and Jump Gates and to avoid all contact with jump holes.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Denver Docking Ring
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TRA data="65281" mask="-31" def="30"/><TEXT>>>>WARNING: Do not attempt planetary landing without using a Docking Ring.<<<</TEXT><PARA/><TRA data="96" mask="-31" def="-1"/><TEXT> </TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>A docking ring is a piece of orbiting technology that, through the use of super strong crystalline polymers and frictionless bearings, assists the smooth atmospheric entry of any interstellar vessel that has the ability to land. Invented in 130 AS by Ageira Technologies, these 'orbital elevators' almost completely negate the cost of boosting people or materials out of a planetary gravity well. Docking rings revolutionized exploration and industry almost overnight, opening up entire systems for commercial exploration and exploitation.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>Ageira Technologies licenses this technology to the other houses, who in turn agree to design all ships (except for special exploratory and survey vessels), to work with the docking ring system.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>Trade lanes are used for superluminal travel within a system. Trade lanes must be entered from their origin point, usually located near key industrial, military, or civilian bases.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>The first trade lane was established through a joint venture between Deep Space Engineering and Ageira Technologies in the year 280 AS. By 350 AS, most of Liberty space was crisscrossed by trade lanes. Through financing from Interspace Commerce, the trade lane network was rapidly extended into the other colonies, helping to create a truly sector-wide economy. Trade lanes are the fastest and safest method of transporting goods and personnel within and between the colonies. Plans to expand the trade lanes to connect interests in the independent territories outside of the colonies are pending.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Hudson Jump Hole
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TRA data="65281" mask="-31" def="30"/><TEXT>***GRAVITATIONAL ANOMALY DETECTED***</TEXT><PARA/><TRA data="96" mask="-31" def="-1"/><TEXT> </TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>Magnetic and gravimetric readings are consistent with a Jump Hole -- a natural phenomenon that functions similar to a Jump Gate, though the hazards associated with traveling through a Jump Hole remain largely unknown. Like Jump Gates, jump holes are semi-permeable areas in real-space that have a tendency to breach the natural boundaries of linear time and space. Unlike Jump Gates, though, these anomalies occur naturally and so are both unpredictable and unstable. Traveling through jump holes is a risky proposition at best. Though some have been charted and, based on accounts from ships that have accidentally encountered them, have had their exit points logged, just as many ships have never been heard from again. It is believed that these ships were either crushed in the violent, cataclysmic vortex that lies outside the narrow corridor of a jump tunnel, or were sent to a place far enough away to make communication or a return trip infeasible. In either case, those missing are presumed dead. Ageira Technologies and Deep Space Engineering urge all citizens to use the prescribed Trade Lanes and Jump Gates and to avoid all contact with jump holes.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Houston Docking Ring
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TRA data="65281" mask="-31" def="30"/><TEXT>>>>WARNING: Do not attempt planetary landing without using a Docking Ring.<<<</TEXT><PARA/><TRA data="96" mask="-31" def="-1"/><TEXT> </TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>A docking ring is a piece of orbiting technology that, through the use of super strong crystalline polymers and frictionless bearings, assists the smooth atmospheric entry of any interstellar vessel that has the ability to land. Invented in 130 AS by Ageira Technologies, these 'orbital elevators' almost completely negate the cost of boosting people or materials out of a planetary gravity well. Docking rings revolutionized exploration and industry almost overnight, opening up entire systems for commercial exploration and exploitation.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>Ageira Technologies licenses this technology to the other houses, who in turn agree to design all ships (except for special exploratory and survey vessels), to work with the docking ring system.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Paul Richards
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>Paul was a middle aged "veteran" of the LPI that had earned his involvement in overseeing much of the security arrangements at the periphery of the site. His Patriot was pulling in to dock, and his colleagues were waiting on the other side of the threshold to surprise him with a birthday cake.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Amy Douglas

When the gate began to malfunction, she tried to escape, hoping her ship could outrun the ensuing blast wave.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>It is clear from the well preserved body behind the canopy that she did not make it.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Alaska -> New York
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>A jump gate is a conveyance technology that allows instantaneous travel between two distinct points in space using technology pioneered by Ageira Technologies and built by Deep Space Engineering in 130 AS. According to the annual Ageira Technologies Shareholder Report, 'jump gate technology is designed to gather and amplify certain permeable tendencies in real-space and connect them to other congruent points elsewhere in the sector, while still maintaining the structural integrity and stability of the channel created by this process and of the object passing through it.'</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>Ageira Technologies and Deep Space Engineering continue to survey other potential jump point candidates and expect to provide connections with other areas further and further away as their research continues.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Supergate
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>The supergate began as a joint project between Deep Space Engineering and Ageira Technologies as Project COLD LAKE -- an attempt at directly connecting Poole and Alberta as a means to bypass the Gallic blockade of Magellan and Cortez. Although initially successful in delivering reinforcements to the Bretonian front, the 826 AS sabotage of the supergate resulted in two Navy battlegroups going missing in transit -- a catastrophe that prompted the gate's immediate shutdown and a formal inquiry from both governmental and corporate angles. The incident prompted a swift response from Ageira, and a team of experts were tasked with painstakingly tracking down the hyperspace signature used to connect the two systems; a gruelling process that eventually resulted in a singular promising result.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>Once the most probable destination of the supergate's jump failure had been pinpointed, Deep Space Engineering and Universal Shipping -- in partnership with Cryer Pharmaceuticals, Ageira Technologies, and Synth Foods Inc. -- were quick to assemble a task force called Expedition Oregon. The concept was simple but bold; a seven-month journey via conventional cruise engines to deliver pre-constructed jump stabilizers that could establish a connection point on the other side, linking the Alaska supergate to the pinpointed destination system. The expedition launched in January of 827, and after months of travel the convoy arrived in Omicron Nu. It took weeks to successfully stabilize the connection between Nu itself and the Alaska system after their arrival; a process that unexpectedly applied itself to the other jump anomalies in the system, linking Omicron Nu to several neighbouring systems as well as Alaska itself. Regardless, their work laid the foundation for finishing the Omicron Nu supergate in its entirety.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>With the COLD LAKE supergate malfunction still fresh in their memories, a separate team of Ageira scientists began cross-referencing their data with archives dating back to the Texas Incident of 500 AS, drawing what parallels they could between the two disasters to ensure a third could never happen. The Alberta supergate was disassembled as quickly as possible and prepared for relocation and reconstruction in Alaska proper -- with a team of Ageira Technologies, Deep Space Engineering, and Universal Shipping working round-the-clock to reassemble the gate under the Liberty government's watchful eye. It took them less than a year to complete the gate and prepare it for initialization -- and when the Oregon expeditioners successfully engaged their jump stabilizers and signalled back to the Alaska team, the connection was rapidly finalised, allowing the Liberty government to begin projecting influence into Omicron Nu with impunity.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Planet Hartford
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>This is the most well paid location for Kishiro research scientists. If we can deliver on our promises, all of Kusari will view us as heroes one day. If we fail, I will enter the airlock and eject myself into the mine field. </TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Planet Stratford
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>I'm a direct descendant of Kishiro, the founder of this company. People murmur that I got this post because of my family, but I have worked hard to get where I am. I was first in my class at New Tokyo University. This was a natural choice to honor my family tradition. </TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Red Station
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>Kishiro is building specialized new Hull Panels under the guise of gas miner production in the Yukawa shipyard. They are also constructing special field generators that are able to fit within a stripped down cruiser. Our goal is to make an instant leap into Sigma-17 from Kansai, without the aid of Jump Gates, less than 10 years from now. </TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Williamstown Wreck
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>Williamstown Depot was hastily constructed in 828 AS as a logistics hub and refueling platform for Liberty's invasion of Kansas. During the campaign against the Liberty Insurgency, Williamstown expanded significantly to keep pace with fleet demands for Munitions, H-Fuel and MOX. Shortly before the Insurgency stronghold of Vespucci was breached, much of the Depot's garrison were drawn away by a large diversionary attack on Philadelphia Station.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>The remaining Liberty Navy fighters were quickly overwhelmed by an Insurgency force of bombers and gunboats which succeeded in detonating Williamstown's fuel tanks, as well as a number of moored fuel tankers. The station was never salvaged, instead being left to fall into Tremont's atmosphere where it will soon burn up. The LSF has long suspected that the attack was facilitated by intelligence provided by local Pennsylvania informants.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Pennsylvania -> New York
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>A jump gate is a conveyance technology that allows instantaneous travel between two distinct points in space using technology pioneered by Ageira Technologies and built by Deep Space Engineering in 130 AS. According to the annual Ageira Technologies Shareholder Report, 'jump gate technology is designed to gather and amplify certain permeable tendencies in real-space and connect them to other congruent points elsewhere in the sector, while still maintaining the structural integrity and stability of the channel created by this process and of the object passing through it.'</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>Ageira Technologies and Deep Space Engineering continue to survey other potential jump point candidates and expect to provide connections with other areas further and further away as their research continues.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Kansas Jump Hole
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TRA data="65281" mask="-31" def="30"/><TEXT>***GRAVITATIONAL ANOMALY DETECTED***</TEXT><PARA/><TRA data="96" mask="-31" def="-1"/><TEXT> </TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>Magnetic and gravimetric readings are consistent with a Jump Hole -- a natural phenomenon that functions similar to a Jump Gate, though the hazards associated with traveling through a Jump Hole remain largely unknown. Like Jump Gates, jump holes are semi-permeable areas in real-space that have a tendency to breach the natural boundaries of linear time and space. Unlike Jump Gates, though, these anomalies occur naturally and so are both unpredictable and unstable. Traveling through jump holes is a risky proposition at best. Though some have been charted and, based on accounts from ships that have accidentally encountered them, have had their exit points logged, just as many ships have never been heard from again. It is believed that these ships were either crushed in the violent, cataclysmic vortex that lies outside the narrow corridor of a jump tunnel, or were sent to a place far enough away to make communication or a return trip infeasible. In either case, those missing are presumed dead. Ageira Technologies and Deep Space Engineering urge all citizens to use the prescribed Trade Lanes and Jump Gates and to avoid all contact with jump holes.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Erie Docking Ring
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TRA data="65281" mask="-31" def="30"/><TEXT>>>>WARNING: Do not attempt planetary landing without using a Docking Ring.<<<</TEXT><PARA/><TRA data="96" mask="-31" def="-1"/><TEXT> </TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>A docking ring is a piece of orbiting technology that, through the use of super strong crystalline polymers and frictionless bearings, assists the smooth atmospheric entry of any interstellar vessel that has the ability to land. Invented in 130 AS by Ageira Technologies, these 'orbital elevators' almost completely negate the cost of boosting people or materials out of a planetary gravity well. Docking rings revolutionized exploration and industry almost overnight, opening up entire systems for commercial exploration and exploitation.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>Ageira Technologies licenses this technology to the other houses, who in turn agree to design all ships (except for special exploratory and survey vessels), to work with the docking ring system.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Inverness Jump Hole
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TRA data="65281" mask="-31" def="30"/><TEXT>***GRAVITATIONAL ANOMALY DETECTED***</TEXT><PARA/><TRA data="96" mask="-31" def="-1"/><TEXT> </TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>Magnetic and gravimetric readings are consistent with a Jump Hole -- a natural phenomenon that functions similar to a Jump Gate, though the hazards associated with traveling through a Jump Hole remain largely unknown. Like Jump Gates, jump holes are semi-permeable areas in real-space that have a tendency to breach the natural boundaries of linear time and space. Unlike Jump Gates, though, these anomalies occur naturally and so are both unpredictable and unstable. Traveling through jump holes is a risky proposition at best. Though some have been charted and, based on accounts from ships that have accidentally encountered them, have had their exit points logged, just as many ships have never been heard from again. It is believed that these ships were either crushed in the violent, cataclysmic vortex that lies outside the narrow corridor of a jump tunnel, or were sent to a place far enough away to make communication or a return trip infeasible. In either case, those missing are presumed dead. Ageira Technologies and Deep Space Engineering urge all citizens to use the prescribed Trade Lanes and Jump Gates and to avoid all contact with jump holes.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Fort Riley Wreck
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>The Insurgency had sufficient reason to believe that a concerted effort was going to be made by a combined Liberty-Bretonia strike group into Vespucci, in order to entirely destroy the holdout.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>However, the unified defensive front drawn from all Insurgency stations would only be met by a light Bretonian attack group, composed of mostly destroyers. With Liberty's own elements nowhere to be seen, thus routing this element proved to be suspiciously easy.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>As a result of this desperate measure, Mulvane and Riley were lacking the garrisons needed to defend themselves from the Delaware's attack group and ultimately both succumbed to an extremely aggressive albeit somewhat costly siege by the Liberty Navy.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Insurgency Cruiser
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TRA bold="true"/><JUST loc="center"/><TEXT>Insurgency "Judicator" Cruiser</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TRA bold="default"/><JUST loc="left"/><TEXT>The third of the new ship projects put into action by Reynard Joyeuse before he departed, the Judicator Cruiser was originally designed with the Insurgency's typical modus operandi in mind - heavy assault. The ship saw several complications in its inception however, and while mass production was put on hold, the Judicator changed to fit the times that the Insurgency was facing.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>Initially built around a massive experimental beam weapon, this system was gutted in favor of expanded fighter facilities, more suited for the Insurgency's more recent patrols of the neighboring systems. Other notable features include a large centrifuge to supply extra power to other systems while still giving quarters of the ship gravity and a redundant engine array system, supposedly nigh impossible to disable.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>Young Legionnaires often breathe a sigh of relief after being assigned to a Judicator as they are most often relegated to backwater patrols, in addition to being considered one of the safer vessels in the Insurgency's arsenal.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: New Berlin Docking Ring
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TRA data="65281" mask="-31" def="30"/><TEXT>>>>WARNING: Do not attempt planetary landing without using a Docking Ring.<<<</TEXT><PARA/><TRA data="96" mask="-31" def="-1"/><TEXT> </TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>A docking ring is a piece of orbiting technology that, through the use of super strong crystalline polymers and frictionless bearings, assists the smooth atmospheric entry of any interstellar vessel that has the ability to land. Invented in 130 AS by Ageira Technologies, these 'orbital elevators' almost completely negate the cost of boosting people or materials out of a planetary gravity well. Docking rings revolutionized exploration and industry almost overnight, opening up entire systems for commercial exploration and exploitation.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>Ageira Technologies licenses this technology to the other houses, who in turn agree to design all ships (except for special exploratory and survey vessels), to work with the docking ring system.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Dortmund Wreck
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>Dortmund Station was the primary processing facility and headquarters of ALG Waste Disposal. Prior to the Rheinland Civil War, ALG had expanded Dortmund into the re-smelting of Scrap Metal and Toxic Waste to produce Alloys and MOX, and were also experimenting with the production of High-Temperature Alloys.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>Following the Imperial coup of 827 AS, ALG's relationship with what they perceived as an illegitimate government soured. As a result, the Imperial Military attempted to capture Dortmund to secure the production of strategically vital MOX.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>This attempt failed however, and the base was scuttled to deny the Imperials their desired fuel source. The wreck was quickly shunted into the Ruhrfeld in the hope of preventing contaminants from leaking out into the lane junction and endangering traffic. So far ALG has shown little interest in taking on the clean-up operation for the station, however the Junkers have done a lively job of picking over its carcass for valuable salvage.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Hamburg -> Bering
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>A jump gate is a conveyance technology that allows instantaneous travel between two distinct points in space using technology pioneered by Ageira Technologies and built by Deep Space Engineering in 130 AS. objects.name: Bering Jump Hole
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TRA data="65281" mask="-31" def="30"/><TEXT>***GRAVITATIONAL ANOMALY DETECTED***</TEXT><PARA/><TRA data="96" mask="-31" def="-1"/><TEXT> </TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>Magnetic and gravimetric readings are consistent with a Jump Hole -- a natural phenomenon that functions similar to a Jump Gate, though the hazards associated with traveling through a Jump Hole remain largely unknown. Like Jump Gates, jump holes are semi-permeable areas in real-space that have a tendency to breach the natural boundaries of linear time and space. Unlike Jump Gates, though, these anomalies occur naturally and so are both unpredictable and unstable. Traveling through jump holes is a risky proposition at best. Though some have been charted and, based on accounts from ships that have accidentally encountered them, have had their exit points logged, just as many ships have never been heard from again. It is believed that these ships were either crushed in the violent, cataclysmic vortex that lies outside the narrow corridor of a jump tunnel, or were sent to a place far enough away to make communication or a return trip infeasible. In either case, those missing are presumed dead. Ageira Technologies and Deep Space Engineering urge all citizens to use the prescribed Trade Lanes and Jump Gates and to avoid all contact with jump holes.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Vierlande Wreck
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>CLASS: Abbey </TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>GRAVITY: N/A</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>DOCKING: No</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>AMENITIES: None</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>CREW: 0</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>INMATES: 0</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>Vierlande Prison was built in 715 AS and breached in 826 AS. For over one hundred years, its extreme conditions made it one of the most dreaded destinations for Rheinland's terrorists and political prisoners. Sentences to Vierlande were almost always for life, with those few discharged forever changed. With the Rheinland Military distracted by the Saigon War, a force consisting of the Coalition, Red Hessians and Unioners took advantage of a lapse in security to capture the station, indiscriminately releasing the thousands of inmates within.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>During the victory celebrations, the Coalition and Red Hessians turned on their former allies, accusing the Unioners of collaboration with the Corsairs. The Coalition Carrier Alvin Katz and Hessian Battleship Zuschen took the Unioner flagship Undine by surprise, destroying it and scattering her escorts. As the Coalition and Hessians withdrew, surviving Unioners reoccupied the Prison. Despite some probing attacks by outgunned RFP patrols, they successfully converted the base into a smuggling way-station, and front line against further Hessian attacks.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>During the Civil War, Imperial forces would turn a blind eye to the Unioner occupation of the prison, seeing them as a useful irregular force. Despite this, tolerance of Unioner piracy would quickly wane, with the post-war armistice offered to the Unioners almost immediately collapsing in 829 AS. In one of the first military operations of the new Consensus Government, the Battleship Kolleda was dispatched to 'deconstruct' the station, with the Unioners hastily retreating rather than fighting the Military head-on.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Undine Wreck
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>CLASS: Bismarck</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>CREW: 0</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>ARMAMENT: N/A</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>The Battleship Undine was deployed in 798 AS during Rheinland's explosive military buildup prior to the Colony Wars. Assigned to the Western Fleet, she was dispatched to the Hamburg border, before pushing into the Bering Independent Worlds on the outbreak of war in 800 AS. The Undine suffered heavy damage to its engines when a temporary refueling depot it was moored to was destroyed by renegade Liberty cruisers. In the chaos of Rheinland's government collapsing soon after, survivors describe the Undine's officers going "berserk" and massacring fellow crewmen, before being overwhelmed. The remaining crew abandoned the immobilized ship using onboard shuttles and fled back to Rheinland. </TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>Drifting inside the Tanner Asteroid Belt, the Undine's location was quickly lost -- it would be many years before Rheinland's authorities were stable enough to dispatch search parties in vain. Instead, the asteroid-battered hulk was rediscovered by Unioner scavengers, who were prowling Colony War battlefields for military grade salvage. After slowly towing the battleship back to Pacifica Base, work began on tearing out internal components and valuable subsystems for use in the development of the early Hel class cruisers. When the Red Hessians launched their first battleship in 819 AS, the Unioners rushed to compete, fearing the Hessian's rising influence and prestige within Rheinland's underworld.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>The stripped hull of the Undine was selected for repair, with the Unioners bartering components from the Junkers of Yanagi and the Corsairs, and scavenging from Thuringia, Bering, and Hudson. The Undine's first major deployment came in 826 AS against the vulnerable Vierlande Prison. The Unioners led a flotilla of Coalition and Red Hessian forces in capturing the station and freeing its inmates. Little did the Unioners know that their "allies" were aware of the Unioners' cooperation with the Corsairs, using the joint assault to spring an ambush that tore the Undine apart. After the shellshocked Unioners re-occupied the Prison, they assessed that the Undine was completely unsalvagable, and could not make a jump back to Bering. As a result, it was once again stripped of components for recycling into other projects.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Karlsruhe Wreck
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>CLASS: Westfalen</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>CREW: N/A</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>ARMAMENT: N/A</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>The Battleship Karlsruhe was completed in 813 AS alongside its sister ships Westfalen and Koblenz. Intended to revitalize the chronically under-equipped Rheinland Military, the Karlsruhe was deployed to Stuttgart in response to escalating LWB and Red Hessian attacks on Planet Stuttgart’s orbit. The Karlsruhe’s Marines were frequently deployed to execute arrest warrants against suspected LWB activists on the planet, leading to complaints from both the sidelined RFP and concerned progressive politicians. The captain of the Karlsruhe traditionally held a well-compensated seat on the Stuttgart Grower’s Association (WVS), while many officers moonlighted as Synth Foods security consultants.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>The battleship saw no significant action until the Rheinland Civil War, avoiding deployment during the Hudson and Saigon Wars thanks to Stuttgart lobbying. Caught entirely unaware by the Imperial coup, the vessel was forced to fight off mutinous elements of its own battlegroup, before fleeing to Cologne to escape the approaching Battleship Altenburg. The Karlsruhe eventually withdrew to Zurich, after being forced from Cologne by the Red Hessian conquest. The Gallic Confederation demanded the Westfalen's internment for the duration of the conflict in an attempt to avoid being drawn into their neighbor’s dispute. Following months of difficult negotiations, the Westfalen’s captain eventually secured resupply and permission to depart, on the terms that the battlegroup only be used to attack the Red Hessians and reopen the Alsace Passage for neutral trade.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>Despite this, the Karlsruhe immediately set a course for Stuttgart, avoiding Red Hessian positions. Having received orders to launch a diversionary attack in support of the Federalist summer offensive of 827 AS, the Karlsruhe’s reappearance immediately drew Imperial reinforcements from New Berlin and the Omegas. In the Battle of the Nordnebel, the Battleships Altenburg and Westfalen finally pinned the Karlsruhe, which ultimately sacrificed itself to enable the survivors of its battlegroup to escape. In the years since the Civil War, ALG has worked to decontaminate the outskirts of the Nordnebel, and recover the most sensitive pieces of military wreckage.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Hamburg Jump Hole
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TRA data="65281" mask="-31" def="30"/><TEXT>***GRAVITATIONAL ANOMALY DETECTED***</TEXT><PARA/><TRA data="96" mask="-31" def="-1"/><TEXT> </TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>Magnetic and gravimetric readings are consistent with a Jump Hole -- a natural phenomenon that functions similar to a Jump Gate, though the hazards associated with traveling through a Jump Hole remain largely unknown. Like Jump Gates, jump holes are semi-permeable areas in real-space that have a tendency to breach the natural boundaries of linear time and space. Unlike Jump Gates, though, these anomalies occur naturally and so are both unpredictable and unstable. Traveling through jump holes is a risky proposition at best. Though some have been charted and, based on accounts from ships that have accidentally encountered them, have had their exit points logged, just as many ships have never been heard from again. It is believed that these ships were either crushed in the violent, cataclysmic vortex that lies outside the narrow corridor of a jump tunnel, or were sent to a place far enough away to make communication or a return trip infeasible. In either case, those missing are presumed dead. Ageira Technologies and Deep Space Engineering urge all citizens to use the prescribed Trade Lanes and Jump Gates and to avoid all contact with jump holes.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Holstein Docking Ring
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TRA data="65281" mask="-31" def="30"/><TEXT>>>>WARNING: Do not attempt planetary landing without using a Docking Ring.<<<</TEXT><PARA/><TRA data="96" mask="-31" def="-1"/><TEXT> </TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>A docking ring is a piece of orbiting technology that, through the use of super strong crystalline polymers and frictionless bearings, assists the smooth atmospheric entry of any interstellar vessel that has the ability to land. Invented in 130 AS by Ageira Technologies, these 'orbital elevators' almost completely negate the cost of boosting people or materials out of a planetary gravity well. Docking rings revolutionized exploration and industry almost overnight, opening up entire systems for commercial exploration and exploitation.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>Ageira Technologies licenses this technology to the other houses, who in turn agree to design all ships (except for special exploratory and survey vessels), to work with the docking ring system.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Leipzig Wreck
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>Once the heart of Daumann ore processing in Dresden, Leipzig was abandoned in 818 AS as viable mining deposits dwindled. While Daumann had evacuated as much of the station's processing machinery to The Ring as was possible, the Red Hessians were still able to put Leipzig's integrated foundries to use for well over a decade.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>What remains of the station now is a twisted, perforated, and half-melted mass of scrap metal. Despite forewarning of Rheinland's impending attack, the Hessians were caught off guard by the diversionary attack into the Giftnebel by the 4th Strike Flotilla. The main Strausberg fleet was barely slowed by Bautzen Station, and closed in on Leipzig rapidly. The station garrison engaged the incoming fleet at the edge of the Innenstadtfeld and awaited reinforcements.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>The Battleship Kassel and its support group were delayed, having first dispatched the attackers pushing into Vogtland's minefield. It was too late to save Leipzig or its defenders, however the Hessians successfully sprung an ambush on the Military fleet in retribution.</TEXT><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Bautzen Wreck
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>Built in 288 AS, Bautzen Station supported Kruger Minerals’ mining operations in Dresden. Smaller than the rival Daumann facility at Leipzig, Kruger focused solely on the extraction of Diamonds from the Schwefelnebel. It is from here that the famous Blue Diamonds -- also known as "Hessian Tears'' -- originated. The vast majority of the Diamonds mined in Dresden were used for industrial drills, as their quality was usually not high enough for luxury markets. Many believed Kruger would abandon the station by 820 AS, owing to failing infrastructure and dwindling Diamond yields. The station received a slight reprieve in 815 AS, when surveyors identified new deposits of Diamonds deeper than ever in the dangerous Schwefelwolke.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>Despite this, the Hessian surge of 818 AS saw Leipzig fall and Pirna Border Station destroyed, with Bautzen only surviving after the Battleship Altenburg routed a large Hessian attack on the base. Kruger was reluctant to abandon Bautzen so soon after discovering a profitable new claim, however the Rheinland government forced the corporation to subsidize the cost of maintaining Dresden’s Military garrison. By 824 AS, Bautzen needed urgent renovations to continue operating. Loathe to invest the needed funds and facing ever increasing security costs, Kruger finally agreed to pull out of the system.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>When several demolition charges failed to detonate, Bundschuh engineers were able to board and make them safe, occupying the station. The Bundschuh put the base to work as a smuggling depot, selling Hessian-refined resources to contacts in the Sigmas to raise funds for both movements. In the aftermath of the Rheinland Civil War, the technically-legalized Bundschuh occupied a tenuous position at Bautzen, which breached Rheinland laws quarantining Dresden. When the Rheinland Military invaded the system in 832 AS, they had little patience for Bundschuh legality -- the Battleship Strausberg razed the station without warning, later claiming to have acted in self-defense after coming under attack.</TEXT><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Strausberg Wreck
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>CLASS: Westfalen</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>CREW: N/A</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>ARMAMENT:  N/A</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>The Battleship Strausberg was completed in 815 AS and deployed to bolster security in New Berlin. During its initial years of service, the Strausberg acquired a reputation for ruthlessness, with a disproportionately high kill to capture ratio against Bundschuh and Red Hessian targets. During the Fall of Dresden in 818 AS, the Strausberg was ordered to prevent “contagion” disorder in Berlin by conducting aggressive anti-Hessian operations in the Saarfield. It departed New Berlin in 825 AS with the outbreak of the Saigon War, where it assisted with the invasion of Sigma-21 and occupation of Planet Saigon. Similar to the Battleship Kolleda, Strausberg initially refused to honor the Sigma Treaty ending the war, only withdrawing to Rheinland when threatened with desertion charges.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>In the days before the Civil War, the Strausberg returned to Oder Shipyard for ‘unscheduled’ maintenance. From there it unsuccessfully attempted to arrest the Federal government, who were instead evacuated by the loyalist Carrier Saar. The Strausberg fired several times on Planet New Berlin during the war, and frequently fought the Saar’s strike wings as they sortied from Frankfurt. Following the Holstein Accords in 828 AS, the Strausberg participated successfully in the Recapture of Cologne, alongside the Battleship Altenburg. Believing the Hessians to be significantly weaker than previously thought, the Strausberg later led Rheinland’s Dresden Campaign in 832 AS.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>The expedition was ambushed by the Hessian Battleship Kassel in the Innenstadtfeld. Despite suffering heavy damage to its reactor plating, the Strausberg’s heavier armament and fleet allowed it to overpower its opponent. The fleet was forced to abandon the attack on Leipzig, initiating a slow retreat towards New Berlin. Near the Bautzen Wreck, the Strausberg again came under heavy assault by Hessian bomber squadrons. These wings successfully landed several torpedoes on the damaged reactor, leading to a critical meltdown. Orders were given to strip and scuttle the ship to prevent it falling into enemy hands. Some in the Military have bitterly complained that the Hessian defense was significantly aided by the operation’s start date being announced by the Emperor at a social event, while gloating about the Hessians’ impending destruction.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Kassel Wreck
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>Battleship Kassel was launched in 820 AS, and initially saw action in Omega-3, 5 and 11. This included tours fighting the Corsairs, and engagements with the Bretonia Armed Forces during the Aland Crisis, notoriously destroying the Gwent in Sprague orbit. The battleship is most famous for its role in the Conquest of Cologne, during which the Red Hessians entirely drove out Rheinland and Bounty Hunter forces. As of 832 AS, the Kassel was still undergoing repairs at Wolfsburg Shipyard for damage inflicted by the Battleship Altenburg during Rheinland’s operation to recapture Cologne. Despite this, it was prematurely pressed back into service with a motley garrison fleet when it became clear Rheinland planned to strike directly at Dresden too.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>When the Battleship Strausberg first launched its attack, the Hessians intended to wear it down through attritional raids as it advanced through the system, with the Kassel finally delivering the killing blow. What the Hessians did not expect was a large diversionary attack into the prepared defenses of the Giftnebel, pinning the Kassel until the 4th Strike Flotilla was repelled. By this point, the Strausberg was bearing down on Leipzig Station, with the Hessian defense forces significantly out of position. While Leipzig was lost, the defenders had succeeded in destroying a number of its cruiser picket ships, denting Rheinland’s sensor perimeter. The Kassel exploited the confusion of battle and the Innenstadtfeld’s treacherous conditions to hit the Strausberg’s column in its exposed flank.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>The Hessian counter-attack initially inflicted heavy damage on the Strausberg, blasting away its reactor shielding and setting several decks ablaze. Despite this, the larger Rheinland fleet was steadily overwhelming their smaller Hessian opponents, and the Kassel’s rushed repairs were beginning to buckle under the strain. After a cascading electrical failure blew out one of the battleship’s engines, it lost the ability to maneuver effectively and was slowly torn to pieces by Military capital ships. The few surviving crewmembers ejected and were rescued by the escort cruiser Dieburg. Despite initial attempts at covering up the Kessel’s loss, the news of the infamous ship’s destruction has since spread, dealing a significant blow to Hessian morale.</TEXT><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Dresden Jump Hole
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TRA data="65281" mask="-31" def="30"/><TEXT>***GRAVITATIONAL ANOMALY DETECTED***</TEXT><PARA/><TRA data="96" mask="-31" def="-1"/><TEXT> </TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>Magnetic and gravimetric readings are consistent with a Jump Hole -- a natural phenomenon that functions similar to a Jump Gate, though the hazards associated with traveling through a Jump Hole remain largely unknown. Like Jump Gates, jump holes are semi-permeable areas in real-space that have a tendency to breach the natural boundaries of linear time and space. Unlike Jump Gates, though, these anomalies occur naturally and so are both unpredictable and unstable. Traveling through jump holes is a risky proposition at best. Though some have been charted and, based on accounts from ships that have accidentally encountered them, have had their exit points logged, just as many ships have never been heard from again. It is believed that these ships were either crushed in the violent, cataclysmic vortex that lies outside the narrow corridor of a jump tunnel, or were sent to a place far enough away to make communication or a return trip infeasible. In either case, those missing are presumed dead. Ageira Technologies and Deep Space Engineering urge all citizens to use the prescribed Trade Lanes and Jump Gates and to avoid all contact with jump holes.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Weimar Docking Ring
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TRA data="65281" mask="-31" def="30"/><TEXT>>>>WARNING: Do not attempt planetary landing without using a Docking Ring.<<<</TEXT><PARA/><TRA data="96" mask="-31" def="-1"/><TEXT> </TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>A docking ring is a piece of orbiting technology that, through the use of super strong crystalline polymers and frictionless bearings, assists the smooth atmospheric entry of any interstellar vessel that has the ability to land. Invented in 130 AS by Ageira Technologies, these 'orbital elevators' almost completely negate the cost of boosting people or materials out of a planetary gravity well. Docking rings revolutionized exploration and industry almost overnight, opening up entire systems for commercial exploration and exploitation.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>Ageira Technologies licenses this technology to the other houses, who in turn agree to design all ships (except for special exploratory and survey vessels), to work with the docking ring system.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Frankfurt Jump Hole
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TRA data="65281" mask="-31" def="30"/><TEXT>***GRAVITATIONAL ANOMALY DETECTED***</TEXT><PARA/><TRA data="96" mask="-31" def="-1"/><TEXT> </TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>Magnetic and gravimetric readings are consistent with a Jump Hole -- a natural phenomenon that functions similar to a Jump Gate, though the hazards associated with traveling through a Jump Hole remain largely unknown. Like Jump Gates, jump holes are semi-permeable areas in real-space that have a tendency to breach the natural boundaries of linear time and space. Unlike Jump Gates, though, these anomalies occur naturally and so are both unpredictable and unstable. Traveling through jump holes is a risky proposition at best. Though some have been charted and, based on accounts from ships that have accidentally encountered them, have had their exit points logged, just as many ships have never been heard from again. It is believed that these ships were either crushed in the violent, cataclysmic vortex that lies outside the narrow corridor of a jump tunnel, or were sent to a place far enough away to make communication or a return trip infeasible. In either case, those missing are presumed dead. Ageira Technologies and Deep Space Engineering urge all citizens to use the prescribed Trade Lanes and Jump Gates and to avoid all contact with jump holes.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Hammersee Docking Ring
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TRA data="65281" mask="-31" def="30"/><TEXT>>>>WARNING: Do not attempt planetary landing without using a Docking Ring.<<<</TEXT><PARA/><TRA data="96" mask="-31" def="-1"/><TEXT> </TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>A docking ring is a piece of orbiting technology that, through the use of super strong crystalline polymers and frictionless bearings, assists the smooth atmospheric entry of any interstellar vessel that has the ability to land. Invented in 130 AS by Ageira Technologies, these 'orbital elevators' almost completely negate the cost of boosting people or materials out of a planetary gravity well. Docking rings revolutionized exploration and industry almost overnight, opening up entire systems for commercial exploration and exploitation.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>Ageira Technologies licenses this technology to the other houses, who in turn agree to design all ships (except for special exploratory and survey vessels), to work with the docking ring system.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: EFL Transport Gaston
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>Tasked with delivering gate construction materials for EFLs gate and lane project in Sigma 15, the Gaston had been conducting task of collecting equipment stored at the Rho gate site for relocation to the Sigma-13 project following issues with the original Frankfurt to Sigma 13 connection. Unfortunately for Gaston, Corsair raiders caught the transport loading supplies at the Rho site, and destroyed its engines before a nearby Bounty Hunter patrol intervened. EFL determined that further relocation was too risky and the fully loaded transport and a considerable field of debris was left behind.</TEXT><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Brilliance
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>The remains of the APM transport vessel christened as Brilliance, which was commanded by the relatively successful captain Charlotte Sterris with Bretonian origins.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>Charlotte Sterris was an outstanding transport captain and was known for several successful blockade runs during the Gallic War. She joined APM once the war ended, selling her skills to the highest bidder around Bretonia.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>The Brilliance became her personal ship and thanks to her blockade running experience, it became a thorn in the Order's and Corsairs' side as they have not been able to intercept her successfully, only losing several fighters when trying to do so.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>But it was not the Order or Corsairs who finally managed to catch her vessel off guard as the wreck bears critical damage caused by alien weaponry. Cut marks around the airlocks suggest that the vessel has been boarded afterwards and there is no whereabouts of what happened with the crew. There is a slight possibility that there still might be valuable cargo onboard.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Iridium Ore
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TRA data="1" mask="1" def="-2"/><JUST loc="center"/><TEXT>IRIDIUM ORE</TEXT><PARA/><TRA data="0" mask="1" def="-1"/><JUST loc="left"/><TEXT> </TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>Iridium is a dense, very hard, brittle, silvery-white transition metal of the platinum family, and is the most corrosion-resistant element known to exist. It is used in multiple commercial applications, from increasing the efficiency of polymers, creating high-temperature alloys for use in fusion reactors and other high-temperature environments, to the production of antimatter and antimatter based weapons. It is a very rare material and its only known abundant source is in the Omicron Delta system.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TRA data="1" mask="1" def="-2"/><JUST loc="center"/><TEXT>Properties</TEXT><PARA/><TRA data="0" mask="1" def="-1"/><PARA/><JUST loc="left"/><TEXT>Base Price: $2</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>Container Hitpoints: 250</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>Cargo Space Per Unit: 2</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>   in Asteroid Miners: 1</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Omicron Delta Jump Hole
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TRA data="65281" mask="-31" def="30"/><TEXT>***GRAVITATIONAL ANOMALY DETECTED***</TEXT><PARA/><TRA data="96" mask="-31" def="-1"/><TEXT> </TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>Magnetic and gravimetric readings are consistent with a Jump Hole -- a natural phenomenon that functions similar to a Jump Gate, though the hazards associated with traveling through a Jump Hole remain largely unknown. Like Jump Gates, jump holes are semi-permeable areas in real-space that have a tendency to breach the natural boundaries of linear time and space. Unlike Jump Gates, though, these anomalies occur naturally and so are both unpredictable and unstable. Traveling through jump holes is a risky proposition at best. Though some have been charted and, based on accounts from ships that have accidentally encountered them, have had their exit points logged, just as many ships have never been heard from again. It is believed that these ships were either crushed in the violent, cataclysmic vortex that lies outside the narrow corridor of a jump tunnel, or were sent to a place far enough away to make communication or a return trip infeasible. In either case, those missing are presumed dead. Ageira Technologies and Deep Space Engineering urge all citizens to use the prescribed Trade Lanes and Jump Gates and to avoid all contact with jump holes.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Alexandria Wreck
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>CLASS: Pharos</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>GRAVITY: No</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>DOCKING: No</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>AMENITIES: No</TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>CREW: 0</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>The remains of Alexandria Research Station, once the most secretive black site of The Order. Established in 810 AS shortly after Order scouts discovered Omicron Mu, Alexandria was mined into a large asteroid within the remote depths of the Wall of Seth. It conducted The Order's most dangerous and unethical experiments under strict quarantine, pursuing an extremist "greater good" ideology that was justified as necessary to prevent humanity's extinction. The black site officially never existed, however many Order pilots whisper of harrowing experiments on live Nomads and infested or enthralled humans. Agents with more lurid imaginations claim Alexandria led Order research into human psionics, allegedly pairing volunteers with active Artifacts, genetic alterations, and mind-altering drugs.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>Alexandria's work came to an abrupt end in 829 AS, when the Kusari Battleship Hakodate launched an unexpected attack from Tohoku, supported by Chochinbi special forces. Appearing at close range thanks to sophisticated cloaking devices, the Kusari attackers quickly overwhelmed the base's small garrison. Before Order reinforcements could arrive, the asteroid was shattered through torpedo strikes and the battleship's bombardment. Fearing a large-scale breach of Alexandria's internal quarantines, the station commander initiated a purge protocol, sending the reactor into an explosive meltdown and killing any survivors. Despite speculation that some research materials may have survived the catastrophe, The Order has not attempted to salvage the radioactive sarcophagus.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Unknown Object
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TRA data="65281" mask="-31" def="30"/><TEXT>***GRAVITATIONAL ANOMALY DETECTED***</TEXT><PARA/><TRA data="96" mask="-31" def="-1"/><TEXT> </TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>Magnetic and gravimetric readings are consistent with a Jump Hole -- a natural phenomenon that functions similar to a Jump Gate, though the hazards associated with traveling through a Jump Hole remain largely unknown. Like Jump Gates, jump holes are semi-permeable areas in real-space that have a tendency to breach the natural boundaries of linear time and space. Unlike Jump Gates, though, these anomalies occur naturally and so are both unpredictable and unstable. Traveling through jump holes is a risky proposition at best. Though some have been charted and, based on accounts from ships that have accidentally encountered them, have had their exit points logged, just as many ships have never been heard from again. It is believed that these ships were either crushed in the violent, cataclysmic vortex that lies outside the narrow corridor of a jump tunnel, or were sent to a place far enough away to make communication or a return trip infeasible. In either case, those missing are presumed dead. Ageira Technologies and Deep Space Engineering urge all citizens to use the prescribed Trade Lanes and Jump Gates and to avoid all contact with jump holes.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>Ammo and equipment isn't so much of a problem on an industrial planet. We can use the factories we still hold to manufacture more. The problem is with the more basic supplies. Consumer Goods used to be ordered in from London, and we were entirely reliant on Cambridge Food Rations. With the seige in place, we've got finite stockpiles that we're having to ration carefully. Once they're gone, things get... interesting. Hopefully the engineers will have some biopods up by then so we can grow stuff here. Much like on spacestations, if you recycle everything, the only thing you need is energy, and that's something we can manage on Leeds. </TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TRA data="65281" mask="-31" def="30"/><TEXT>***GRAVITATIONAL ANOMALY DETECTED***</TEXT><PARA/><TRA data="96" mask="-31" def="-1"/><TEXT> </TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>Magnetic and gravimetric readings are consistent with a Jump Hole -- a natural phenomenon that functions similar to a Jump Gate, though the hazards associated with traveling through a Jump Hole remain largely unknown. Like Jump Gates, jump holes are semi-permeable areas in real-space that have a tendency to breach the natural boundaries of linear time and space. Unlike Jump Gates, though, these anomalies occur naturally and so are both unpredictable and unstable. Traveling through jump holes is a risky proposition at best. Though some have been charted and, based on accounts from ships that have accidentally encountered them, have had their exit points logged, just as many ships have never been heard from again. It is believed that these ships were either crushed in the violent, cataclysmic vortex that lies outside the narrow corridor of a jump tunnel, or were sent to a place far enough away to make communication or a return trip infeasible. In either case, those missing are presumed dead. Ageira Technologies and Deep Space Engineering urge all citizens to use the prescribed Trade Lanes and Jump Gates and to avoid all contact with jump holes.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Leeds -> New London
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>A jump gate is a conveyance technology that allows instantaneous travel between two distinct points in space using technology pioneered by Ageira Technologies and built by Deep Space Engineering in 130 AS. <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TRA data="65281" mask="-31" def="30"/><TEXT>>>>WARNING: Do not attempt planetary landing without using a Docking Ring.<<<</TEXT><PARA/><TRA data="96" mask="-31" def="-1"/><TEXT> </TEXT><PARA/><TEXT>A docking ring is a piece of orbiting technology that, through the use of super strong crystalline polymers and frictionless bearings, assists the smooth atmospheric entry of any interstellar vessel that has the ability to land. Invented in 130 AS by Ageira Technologies, these 'orbital elevators' almost completely negate the cost of boosting people or materials out of a planetary gravity well. Docking rings revolutionized exploration and industry almost overnight, opening up entire systems for commercial exploration and exploitation.</TEXT><PARA/><PARA/><TEXT>Ageira Technologies licenses this technology to the other houses, who in turn agree to design all ships (except for special exploratory and survey vessels), to work with the docking ring system.</TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>

objects.name: Mooring Fixture
objects.infocard: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?><RDL><PUSH/><TEXT>A mooring fixture is a temporary resting area for idle ships within active shipping zones, allowing transports and other large vessels to be unloaded and passengers transferred.  </TEXT><PARA/><POP/></RDL>
